32	
33	**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows.
34	
35	**[ARTICLE II --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**
36	
37	As used in this Treaty, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Terms not otherwise defined herein shall have their commonly understood meaning in the insurance and reinsurance industry.
38	
39	**2.1 \"Business Day\"** means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in both Columbus, Ohio and Hamilton, Bermuda.
40	
41	**2.2 \"Ceded Percentage\"** means forty percent (40%).
42	
43	**2.3 \"Ceding Commission\"** means thirty-two percent (32%) of Ceded Premium, payable by the Reinsurer to the Company in accordance with Article VI, Section 6.2 of this Treaty. The Ceding Commission is intended to reimburse the Company for policy acquisition costs, underwriting expenses, and administrative costs incurred in connection with the business ceded hereunder.
44	
45	**2.4 \"Ceded Premium\"** means the Ceded Percentage applied to the Subject Premium for Treaty-Eligible Lines. Ceded Premium shall be calculated on the basis of Subject Premium as defined in Section 2.16 below.
46	
47	**2.5 \"Company\" or \"Cedent\"** means Blackwater Mutual Insurance Company, a mutual insurance company organized and existing under the laws of the State of Ohio, with its principal office at 2200 Scioto Boulevard, Columbus, OH 43215.
48	
49	**2.6 \"Effective Date\"** means January 1, 2024, at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Standard Time.
50	
51	**2.7 \"Expiration Date\"** means December 31, 2025, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Standard Time.
52	
53	**2.8 \"Extra-Contractual Obligations\" or \"ECO\"** means any loss, damage, or expense (including but not limited to punitive, exemplary, or compensatory damages) arising from the handling of any claim or loss covered or alleged to be covered under an Underlying Policy, which loss, damage, or expense arises from the Company\'s alleged or actual bad faith, failure to settle, fraud, or negligence in the investigation, defense, trial, or settlement of any claim. Extra-Contractual Obligations shall include but not be limited to liability for penalties imposed by regulatory authorities in connection with the handling of claims under Underlying Policies. For the avoidance of doubt, ECO shall not include ordinary claim adjustment expenses or allocated loss adjustment expenses incurred in the normal course of handling claims.
54	
55	**2.9 \"Excess of Policy Limits\" or \"XPL\"** means any loss paid or payable by the Company in excess of the applicable per-occurrence or aggregate limit(s) of an Underlying Policy, where such excess payment results from the Company\'s alleged or actual failure to settle within policy limits. XPL shall be calculated as the amount by which the Company\'s total payment in respect of a claim or Occurrence exceeds the applicable per-occurrence or aggregate limit(s) of the Underlying Policy.
56	
57	**2.10 \"Gross Written Premium\"** means the gross premium (before deduction for cessions to any reinsurer) written, charged, or received by the Company on Treaty-Eligible Lines during the Treaty Period. Gross Written Premium shall include all endorsement premiums, audit premiums, and return premiums, but shall not include any premium taxes or surcharges imposed by any governmental authority.
58	
59	**2.11 \"Net Retained Lines\"** means the percentage of each risk retained by the Company for its own account after all cessions under this Treaty, which shall not be less than fifty percent (50%) of each ceded risk. For the avoidance of doubt, the Company\'s retention under this Treaty is sixty percent (60%) of each risk ceded hereunder.
60	
61	**2.12 \"Occurrence\"** means each individual loss event as determined by the Hours Clause set forth in Section 2.13 of this Treaty. All individual losses arising from a continuous or related cause within any consecutive period of seventy-two (72) hours, as selected by the Company in accordance with Section 2.13, shall constitute a single Occurrence for all purposes under this Treaty.
62	
63	**2.13 \"Hours Clause\" (72-Hour Clause)** means that all individual losses arising from a continuous or related cause within any consecutive period of seventy-two (72) hours shall be deemed a single Occurrence for all purposes under this Treaty, including for the application of the Per-Occurrence Cap. The Company shall select the seventy-two (72) hour period that results in the greatest amount of ceded loss recoverable under this Treaty. Only those individual losses falling within the selected seventy-two (72) hour period shall be included within that Occurrence. The Company shall notify the Reinsurer of the selected seventy-two (72) hour period in writing within a reasonable time after the determination of such period.
64	
65	**2.14 \"Per-Occurrence Cap\"** means Twenty-Five Million United States Dollars (US \$25,000,000), being the maximum liability of the Reinsurer for any single Occurrence under this Treaty. The Per-Occurrence Cap shall apply to the aggregate of all ceded losses arising from a single Occurrence as defined in Sections 2.12 and 2.13 above, inclusive of all loss, loss adjustment expense, and related costs that are otherwise ceded under the terms of this Treaty.
66	
67	**2.15 \"Reinsurer\"** means Pinnacle Re Ltd., a Class 4 licensed insurer under the Bermuda Insurance Act 1978, with its registered office at 14 Church Street, Hamilton HM 11, Bermuda.
68	
69	**2.16 \"Subject Premium\"** means Gross Written Premium for Treaty-Eligible Lines, excluding any premium attributable to supplementary or additional coverage amounts that are payable in addition to the per-occurrence or aggregate limits of an Underlying Policy. For the avoidance of doubt, premiums allocated to coverage extensions that provide amounts in addition to the scheduled policy limits shall not be included in Subject Premium.
70	
71	**2.17 \"Treaty-Eligible Lines\"** means all commercial property risks written by the Company in the Treaty Territory on Underlying Policies with per-occurrence limits not exceeding Seventy-Five Million United States Dollars (US \$75,000,000). Treaty-Eligible Lines include the lines of business enumerated in Schedule A attached hereto.
72	
73	**2.18 \"Treaty Period\"** means the period from and including the Effective Date through and including the Expiration Date.
74	
75	**2.19 \"Treaty Territory\"** means the States of Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky, and West Virginia. For purposes of this Treaty, a risk shall be deemed located within the Treaty Territory if the insured property is situated within one of the four states listed in this Section 2.19 at the time of the inception of the Underlying Policy.
76	
77	**2.20 \"Underlying Policy\"** means any policy of insurance issued by the Company within the Treaty-Eligible Lines during the Treaty Period, covering risks located within the Treaty Territory.
78	
79	**[ARTICLE III --- SCOPE OF TREATY AND BASIS OF CESSION]{.underline}**
80	
81	**3.1 Risks Attaching Basis.** This Treaty is written on a \"risks attaching\" basis. The Reinsurer shall indemnify the Company in respect of its net loss under each Underlying Policy incepting during the Treaty Period, regardless of whether the loss or claim is reported, occurs, or is paid during or after the Treaty Period. For the avoidance of doubt, this Treaty shall apply to all Underlying Policies that incept (i.e., have their policy effective date) during the Treaty Period, and the Reinsurer\'s liability under this Treaty shall extend to all losses arising under such Underlying Policies until all claims thereunder have been finally settled or otherwise resolved, irrespective of whether such settlement or resolution occurs after the Expiration Date.
82	
83	**3.2 Cession.** The Company shall cede, and the Reinsurer shall accept, forty percent (40%) of the Company\'s liability on each and every risk within the Treaty-Eligible Lines, subject to the terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations of this Treaty. The Reinsurer\'s share of each ceded risk shall be proportional to the Ceded Percentage, applied to the Company\'s gross liability under each Underlying Policy. The Reinsurer shall share proportionally in the premiums, losses, loss adjustment expenses, and other amounts attributable to the ceded business, in accordance with the provisions of this Treaty.
84	
85	**3.3 Automatic Cession.** Cession under this Treaty is automatic and obligatory. All Treaty-Eligible Lines shall be ceded without individual risk underwriting approval by the Reinsurer, and the Reinsurer shall not have the right to decline any individual risk within the Treaty-Eligible Lines. The Company shall not be required to submit individual risk information to the Reinsurer prior to cession, but shall provide such information through the bordereaux and reporting procedures set forth in Article VII of this Treaty.
86	
87	**3.4 Net Retained Lines.** The Company shall retain for its own account not less than fifty percent (50%) of each risk ceded hereunder. The Company\'s retention on each risk ceded under this Treaty shall be sixty percent (60%) of the Company\'s gross liability under the applicable Underlying Policy, after giving effect to the forty percent (40%) cession to the Reinsurer. The Company warrants that it shall not cede any portion of its retained share under this Treaty to any other reinsurer except under its existing excess of loss reinsurance program, the details of which shall be disclosed to the Reinsurer upon request.
88	
89	**3.5 Per-Occurrence Cap.** Notwithstanding the Ceded Percentage, the Reinsurer\'s maximum liability in respect of any single Occurrence shall not exceed Twenty-Five Million United States Dollars (US \$25,000,000). In the event that the Reinsurer\'s proportional share of any single Occurrence (calculated at the Ceded Percentage) exceeds the Per-Occurrence Cap, the excess amount above the Per-Occurrence Cap shall revert to the Company and shall be borne by the Company for its own account. For illustrative purposes, if the Company\'s gross loss from a single Occurrence exceeds Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (US \$62,500,000), the Reinsurer\'s proportional share at forty percent (40%) would exceed the Per-Occurrence Cap, and the amount in excess of Twenty-Five Million United States Dollars (US \$25,000,000) would revert to the Company.
90	
91	**3.6 Treaty Territory.** This Treaty shall apply only to risks located in the Treaty Territory, as defined in Section 2.19 of this Treaty. Risks or portions of risks located outside the Treaty Territory are not covered hereunder. Where an Underlying Policy covers property located both within and outside the Treaty Territory, only that portion of the risk attributable to property located within the Treaty Territory shall be ceded under this Treaty. The Company shall allocate premium, losses, and loss adjustment expenses between Treaty Territory and non-Treaty Territory exposures on a reasonable and equitable basis, consistent with the Company\'s customary underwriting and accounting practices.
92	
93	**[ARTICLE IV --- BUSINESS COVERED AND COVERAGE LIMITATIONS]{.underline}**
94	
95	**4.1 Lines of Business.** This Treaty covers all commercial property risks written by the Company within the Treaty Territory, including but not limited to: building coverage, business personal property coverage, business interruption and loss of income coverage (subject to Section 4.2 below), equipment breakdown coverage, and such other coverages as are customarily included within commercial property insurance policies issued by the Company. The specific lines of business covered under this Treaty are enumerated in Schedule A attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference. The Company shall notify the Reinsurer promptly of any material change in the lines of business written by the Company within the Treaty-Eligible Lines.
96	
97	**4.2 Business Interruption Limitation.** Coverage under this Treaty for business interruption or loss of income (including but not limited to loss of business income, extra expense, and contingent business interruption) shall be limited to losses arising from an indemnity period not exceeding six (6) months from the date of the Occurrence giving rise to such loss. Any business interruption or loss of income loss attributable to the period beyond six (6) months from the date of the Occurrence shall not be recoverable under this Treaty and shall be retained in full by the Company for its own account. This limitation applies regardless of the indemnity period specified in the applicable Underlying Policy. The Company acknowledges that this six-month limitation is a material term of this Treaty and has been reflected in the calculation of the Ceding Commission set forth in Section 6.2.
98	
99	**4.3 Underlying Policy Sublimits.** Where an Underlying Policy provides coverage subject to sublimits (whether per-occurrence sublimits, aggregate sublimits, or otherwise), the Reinsurer\'s liability under this Treaty shall not exceed the Ceded Percentage of the applicable sublimit for such coverage under the Underlying Policy. The Reinsurer shall not be liable for any amount in excess of the Ceded Percentage of the applicable sublimit, regardless of the total loss incurred by the Company. For the avoidance of doubt, the Reinsurer\'s liability for each coverage category shall be determined by reference to the sublimit applicable to such category under the Underlying Policy, not by reference to the overall per-occurrence limit of the Underlying Policy.
100	
101	**4.4 Per-Occurrence Limit on Underlying Policies.** This Treaty applies only to Underlying Policies with per-occurrence limits not exceeding Seventy-Five Million United States Dollars (US \$75,000,000). The Company shall not cede under this Treaty any Underlying Policy, or any portion of any Underlying Policy, with a per-occurrence limit in excess of Seventy-Five Million United States Dollars (US \$75,000,000). If the Company issues an Underlying Policy with a per-occurrence limit in excess of such amount, such policy shall not be within the Treaty-Eligible Lines and shall not be ceded under this Treaty.
102	
103	**[ARTICLE V --- EXCLUSIONS]{.underline}**
104	
105	The following exclusions shall apply to this Treaty. The Reinsurer shall have no liability under this Treaty for any loss, damage, expense, or liability arising out of, resulting from, caused by, contributed to by, or in any way connected with any of the following:
106	
107	**5.1 Terrorism.** This Treaty does not cover any loss or liability arising out of, resulting from, caused by, contributed to by, or in any way connected with an act of terrorism as defined under the Terrorism Risk Insurance Act of 2002 (TRIA), as amended by the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Reauthorization Act of 2007 and the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Reauthorization Act of 2015, or any successor legislation thereto, regardless of any other cause or event contributing concurrently or in any other sequence to the loss. This exclusion applies regardless of whether the act of terrorism is certified or not certified by the Secretary of the Treasury of the United States, and regardless of whether the loss is otherwise covered under the Underlying Policy.
108	
109	**5.2 Cyber and Electronic Risks.** This Treaty does not cover any loss or liability arising out of, resulting from, caused by, contributed to by, or in any way connected with: (a) any unauthorized access to or use of any computer system, including any unauthorized access to or use of any data stored on, processed by, or transmitted by any computer system; (b) any denial-of-service attack, distributed denial-of-service attack, or other form of electronic attack directed at any computer system; (c) any malicious code, virus, worm, Trojan horse, ransomware, or similar malicious or destructive code, program, or instruction; (d) any failure of any computer system, software, program, process, or electronic device, whether or not caused by the acts described in subsections (a) through (c) above; or (e) any erasure, destruction, corruption, misappropriation, or manipulation of electronic data or information. This exclusion applies regardless of any other cause or event contributing concurrently or in any other sequence to the loss, and regardless of whether the loss manifests as physical damage to tangible property.
110	
111	**5.3 War and Nuclear.** This Treaty does not cover any loss or liability arising out of, resulting from, caused by, contributed to by, or in any way connected with: (a) war (whether declared or undeclared), invasion, act of foreign enemies, hostilities, warlike operations, civil war, rebellion, revolution, insurrection, military or usurped power, martial law, or confiscation by order of any government or public authority; or (b) nuclear reaction, nuclear radiation, or radioactive contamination, regardless of the cause thereof, including any nuclear weapon, nuclear device, nuclear reactor, or nuclear waste. This exclusion applies regardless of any other cause or event contributing concurrently or in any other sequence to the loss.
112	
113	**5.4 Asbestos and Environmental Pollution.** This Treaty does not cover any loss or liability arising out of, resulting from, caused by, contributed to by, or in any way connected with: (a) the manufacture, mining, processing, distribution, testing, remediation, removal, storage, disposal, sale, use of, or exposure to asbestos or asbestos-containing materials of any kind or nature; or (b) the actual, alleged, or threatened discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release, escape, generation, or disposal of pollutants, contaminants, or hazardous substances into or upon land, the atmosphere, or any watercourse or body of water, whether above or below ground; **provided, however**, that this exclusion shall not apply to loss or liability arising from pollution that is sudden and accidental in nature. The determination of whether pollution is sudden and accidental shall be made on the facts and circumstances of each individual claim. This exception to the pollution exclusion shall not be construed to provide coverage broader than that provided under the applicable Underlying Policy.
114	
115	**5.5 Flood and Earthquake.** This Treaty does not cover any loss or liability arising out of, resulting from, caused by, contributed to by, or in any way connected with: (a) flood, including but not limited to surface water, waves, tides, tidal waves, tsunami, overflow of any body of water, or spray from any of the foregoing, whether driven by wind or not; (b) storm surge, whether or not accompanying a named storm or hurricane; or (c) earthquake, including tremor, seaquake, volcanic eruption, or any earth movement, subsidence, sinkhole, landslide, mudslide, or mudflow. This exclusion applies regardless of any other cause or event contributing concurrently or in any other sequence to the loss, and regardless of whether the applicable Underlying Policy provides coverage for flood or earthquake perils under any sublimit, endorsement, or coverage extension.
116	
117	**5.6 Governmental Action or Order.** This Treaty does not cover any loss or liability arising out of, resulting from, caused by, contributed to by, or in any way connected with any action, order, directive, regulation, decree, or mandate of any governmental, public, municipal, regulatory, or other authority, including but not limited to confiscation, nationalization, seizure, detention, embargo, quarantine, condemnation, or destruction by order of any governmental authority. This exclusion applies regardless of the purpose or objective of such governmental action, order, directive, or regulation, and regardless of whether the applicable Underlying Policy provides coverage for losses arising from compliance with governmental directives.
118	
119	**5.7 Workers\' Compensation.** This Treaty does not cover any loss or liability under any workers\' compensation or employers\' liability insurance policy or program, or any loss or liability arising out of or in connection with any obligation imposed by workers\' compensation, occupational disease, unemployment compensation, or disability benefits law, or any similar law.
120	
121	**[ARTICLE VI --- PREMIUM]{.underline}**
122	
123	**6.1 Ceded Premium.** The Company shall cede to the Reinsurer an amount equal to the Ceded Percentage (40%) of the Subject Premium on Treaty-Eligible Lines during the Treaty Period. Ceded Premium shall be calculated on Subject Premium as defined in Section 2.16 of this Treaty, which excludes premium attributable to supplementary or additional coverage amounts that are payable in addition to the per-occurrence or aggregate limits of an Underlying Policy. The Company shall maintain records sufficient to identify and segregate the premium attributable to supplementary or additional coverage amounts from the Subject Premium.
124	
125	**6.2 Ceding Commission.** The Reinsurer shall pay the Company a ceding commission equal to thirty-two percent (32%) of Ceded Premium. The ceding commission is intended to reimburse the Company for policy acquisition costs (including but not limited to commissions paid to agents and brokers), underwriting expenses, administrative costs, and other overhead expenses incurred in connection with the origination and servicing of the business ceded hereunder. The ceding commission shall be calculated and paid on each quarterly premium settlement in accordance with Section 6.4 below.
126	
127	**6.3 Estimated Premium.** For the fiscal year ending December 31, 2024, the estimated Gross Written Premium for Treaty-Eligible Lines is Two Hundred Fifteen Million United States Dollars (US \$215,000,000), producing the following estimated amounts:
128	
129	  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
130	  **Item**                                                  **Amount**
131	  --------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------
132	  Estimated Gross Written Premium (Treaty-Eligible Lines)   \$215,000,000
133	
134	  Ceded Percentage                                          40%
135	
136	  Estimated Ceded Premium                                   \$86,000,000
137	
138	  Ceding Commission Rate                                    32%
139	
140	  Estimated Ceding Commission                               \$27,520,000
141	
142	  Estimated Net Premium to Reinsurer                        \$58,480,000
143	  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
144	
145	The above estimates are provided for planning and accounting purposes only and are not binding on either party. Actual amounts shall be determined based on the Company\'s actual Gross Written Premium during the Treaty Period.
146	
147	**6.4 Premium Payment.** Ceded Premium (net of Ceding Commission) shall be paid in quarterly installments within forty-five (45) days following the end of each calendar quarter during the Treaty Period, based on the Company\'s bordereaux of ceded business for such quarter as furnished in accordance with Article VII of this Treaty. Each quarterly payment shall reflect the Ceded Premium written during the immediately preceding calendar quarter, less the Ceding Commission applicable thereto.
148	
149	**6.5 Premium Adjustment.** Within ninety (90) days after the end of each calendar year during the Treaty Period, the Company shall provide the Reinsurer with a final premium statement reconciling estimated premium against actual Gross Written Premium for Treaty-Eligible Lines for such calendar year. Any adjustment (whether additional premium owed by the Company to the Reinsurer or return premium owed by the Reinsurer to the Company) shall be settled within thirty (30) days of the Reinsurer\'s receipt of such reconciliation statement. In the event of a dispute regarding the premium adjustment, the parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to resolve such dispute, and any undisputed amounts shall be settled pending resolution of the disputed amounts.
150	
151	**6.6 Offset.** The Company may offset any balance due from it to the Reinsurer under this Treaty against any balance due from the Reinsurer to the Company under this Treaty, whether on account of premiums, losses, commissions, or any other amounts. Such right of offset is available solely to the Company and may be exercised at any time, whether or not the amounts offset are due and payable and whether or not the obligation of either party to the other arises under the same or a different provision of this Treaty. The Company shall provide the Reinsurer with a written statement of any offset within fifteen (15) Business Days of exercising such right.
152	
153	**[ARTICLE VII --- REPORTS AND ACCOUNTS]{.underline}**
154	
155	**7.1 Bordereaux.** The Company shall furnish the Reinsurer with quarterly bordereaux of all ceded business within forty-five (45) days following the end of each calendar quarter during the Treaty Period, setting forth for each Underlying Policy ceded during such quarter the following information: (a) policy number; (b) name of insured; (c) location of risk; (d) policy effective and expiration dates; (e) per-occurrence limit; (f) applicable sublimits; (g) gross premium written; (h) ceded premium; (i) type of coverage; and (j) such other information as the Reinsurer may reasonably request from time to time. The bordereaux shall be furnished in a format mutually agreed upon by the parties or, absent such agreement, in the format customarily used by the Company for reinsurance reporting purposes.
156	
157	**7.2 Loss Bordereaux.** The Company shall furnish the Reinsurer with quarterly loss bordereaux within forty-five (45) days following the end of each calendar quarter during the Treaty Period, setting forth for each reported claim the following information: (a) claim number; (b) policy number; (c) name of insured; (d) date of loss; (e) date of report; (f) nature of loss; (g) gross incurred loss (comprising paid and outstanding amounts separately identified); (h) ceded incurred loss; (i) any applicable salvage or subrogation; and (j) such other information as the Reinsurer may reasonably request from time to time. The loss bordereaux shall continue to be furnished quarterly until all claims arising under Underlying Policies ceded under this Treaty have been finally settled or otherwise resolved.
158	
159	**7.3 Annual Statement.** The Company shall provide the Reinsurer with a copy of the Company\'s annual statutory financial statement as filed with the Ohio Department of Insurance, within thirty (30) days of such filing. In addition, the Company shall provide the Reinsurer with a copy of any quarterly statutory financial statements filed with the Ohio Department of Insurance within thirty (30) days of such filings, upon the Reinsurer\'s written request.
160	
161	**7.4 Additional Information.** The Company shall provide the Reinsurer with such additional reports, data, or information as the Reinsurer may reasonably request from time to time in connection with the business ceded under this Treaty, provided that such requests are not unduly burdensome to the Company.
162	
163	**[ARTICLE VIII --- CLAIMS]{.underline}**
164

Such notice shall be given within fifteen (15) Business Days of the Company\'s receipt of notice of such claim or Occurrence from the insured under the Underlying Policy, or within fifteen (15) Business Days of the Company otherwise becoming aware of such claim or Occurrence, whichever is earlier. **8.5 Loss Payments.** The Reinsurer shall pay its share of losses promptly upon receipt of satisfactory proof of loss from the Company. The Reinsurer shall pay its proportion (the Ceded Percentage) of each loss, loss adjustment expense, and related cost, subject to the Per-Occurrence Cap set forth in Section 3.5 and the exclusions and limitations of this Treaty. Payment shall be made within thirty (30) days of the Reinsurer\'s receipt of such proof of loss, or such shorter period as may be required under applicable law. The Company shall pursue all reasonable salvage and subrogation opportunities and shall not waive any rights of salvage or subrogation without the prior written consent of the Reinsurer, except as may be required by the terms of the applicable Underlying Policy.

**[ARTICLE IX --- EXTRA-CONTRACTUAL OBLIGATIONS AND EXCESS OF POLICY LIMITS]{.underline}**

**9.1 ECO Coverage.** The Reinsurer shall indemnify the Company for Extra-Contractual Obligations (as defined in Section 2.8) arising out of claims covered or alleged to be covered under Underlying Policies, but only to the extent that the underlying loss (exclusive of the ECO amount) falls within the terms of this Treaty. The Reinsurer\'s share of ECO shall be determined by applying the Ceded Percentage to the amount of ECO, subject to the cap set forth in Section 9.3 below. ECO amounts shall be in addition to and not part of the loss under the applicable Underlying Policy for purposes of determining the Reinsurer\'s liability under this Treaty.

**9.2 XPL Coverage.** The Reinsurer shall indemnify the Company for Excess of Policy Limits losses (as defined in Section 2.9) arising out of claims covered or alleged to be covered under Underlying Policies, but only to the extent that the underlying loss (exclusive of the XPL amount) falls within the terms of this Treaty. The Reinsurer\'s share of XPL shall be determined by applying the Ceded Percentage to the amount of XPL, subject to the cap set forth in Section 9.3 below. XPL amounts shall be in addition to and not part of the loss under the applicable Underlying Policy for purposes of determining the Reinsurer\'s liability under this Treaty.

**9.3 ECO/XPL Cap.** The Reinsurer\'s maximum liability for Extra-Contractual Obligations and Excess of Policy Limits losses combined shall not exceed Ten Million United States Dollars (US \$10,000,000) per Occurrence. This cap is separate from and in addition to the Per-Occurrence Cap set forth in Section 3.5. For the avoidance of doubt, the Reinsurer\'s total exposure under this Treaty for any single Occurrence shall not exceed the Per-Occurrence Cap of Twenty-Five Million United States Dollars (US \$25,000,000) for covered losses plus Ten Million United States Dollars (US \$10,000,000) for ECO and XPL combined, for a maximum aggregate exposure of Thirty-Five Million United States Dollars (US \$35,000,000) per Occurrence.

**9.4 Conditions.** ECO and XPL coverage under this Article is contingent upon the Company having acted in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner in the handling, investigation, defense, and settlement of the underlying claim. Coverage under this Article shall not apply where the Extra-Contractual Obligations or Excess of Policy Limits losses result from the Company\'s willful misconduct or fraudulent acts. The Company shall notify the Reinsurer of any potential ECO or XPL claim within fifteen (15) Business Days of the Company becoming aware of any circumstances giving rise to such potential claim. The Reinsurer shall have the right to associate with the Company in the defense of any ECO or XPL claim, in accordance with the procedures set forth in Section 8.2, mutatis mutandis.

**[ARTICLE X --- ARBITRATION]{.underline}**

**10.1 Arbitration Requirement.** Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Treaty, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof, which the parties are unable to resolve through good-faith negotiations within sixty (60) days of written notice of such dispute by one party to the other, shall be finally resolved by arbitration in accordance with the provisions of the Bermuda International Conciliation and Arbitration Act 1993 (the \"BICA Act\"), as amended from time to time. The arbitration shall be conducted in accordance with the BICA Act and the procedural rules agreed upon by the arbitral tribunal, to the extent not inconsistent with the provisions of this Article.

**10.2 Seat of Arbitration.** The juridical seat of arbitration shall be Hamilton, Bermuda. Hearings may be held at such other location(s) as the arbitral tribunal may determine in its discretion, provided that the seat of arbitration shall remain Hamilton, Bermuda for all legal and procedural purposes.

**10.3 Composition of Tribunal.** The arbitral tribunal shall consist of three (3) arbitrators. Each party shall appoint one (1) arbitrator within thirty (30) days of the delivery of the notice of arbitration by the initiating party. The two party-appointed arbitrators shall select a third arbitrator, who shall serve as chair of the tribunal, within thirty (30) days of the appointment of the second arbitrator. If the two party-appointed arbitrators fail to agree on a third arbitrator within such thirty (30) day period, the third arbitrator shall be appointed by the President of the Bermuda Chamber of Commerce upon the written application of either party. The appointment of the third arbitrator by the President of the Bermuda Chamber of Commerce shall be final and binding on the parties.

**10.4 Qualifications.** Each arbitrator shall be a disinterested person who is a current or former officer of an insurance or reinsurance company, or an attorney, actuary, or other professional with not less than ten (10) years of experience in the insurance or reinsurance industry. No arbitrator shall be a current or former employee, officer, director, or consultant of either party, or of any affiliate of either party. Each arbitrator shall disclose to the parties any circumstance that might give rise to justifiable doubt as to the arbitrator\'s impartiality or independence.

**10.5 Honorable Engagement.** The arbitral tribunal shall consider the custom and practice of the insurance and reinsurance industry in interpreting and applying the provisions of this Treaty. The tribunal shall make its award with a view to effecting the general purpose of this Treaty and the honorable engagement of the parties hereto, rather than being constrained by a strict interpretation of the letter of this Treaty. The tribunal shall not award punitive, exemplary, or treble damages unless such damages are required by applicable mandatory law.

**10.6 Costs.** Each party shall bear the fees and expenses of the arbitrator it appoints and its own legal and other costs of the arbitration, including but not limited to the costs of witnesses, experts, and travel. The fees and expenses of the chair and any institutional or administrative fees shall be borne equally by the parties, unless the tribunal directs otherwise in its award.

**10.7 Award.** The award of the tribunal shall be in writing, shall state the reasons for the award in sufficient detail to explain the tribunal\'s findings and conclusions, and shall be final and binding on the parties. The award shall be rendered within sixty (60) days of the close of the hearing, unless the tribunal determines that additional time is necessary and so notifies the parties. Judgment upon any award rendered by the tribunal may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof, including any court in Bermuda, the United States, or any other jurisdiction where enforcement may be sought.

**10.8 Confidentiality.** All proceedings, evidence, submissions, and awards in connection with any arbitration under this Article shall be kept strictly confidential by the parties, their counsel, and the tribunal. Neither party shall disclose the existence or content of any arbitration proceeding to any third party, except as may be required by applicable law, regulation, or court order, or as necessary for the enforcement of any award, or as required by applicable regulatory or supervisory authorities. The tribunal shall have the power to issue protective orders to preserve the confidentiality of the proceedings.

**[ARTICLE XI --- INSOLVENCY]{.underline}**

**11.1 Reinsurer\'s Obligations.** In the event of the insolvency of the Company, the Reinsurer\'s obligations under this Treaty shall be payable directly to the Company or to the liquidator, rehabilitator, receiver, conservator, or statutory successor of the Company, on the basis of the liability of the Company under the Underlying Policies without diminution because of the insolvency of the Company or because the liquidator, rehabilitator, receiver, conservator, or statutory successor of the Company has failed to pay all or a portion of any claim. It is agreed that payment shall be made by the Reinsurer on the basis of claims presented by the liquidator, rehabilitator, receiver, conservator, or statutory successor of the Company, and shall be subject to the applicable court order or orders entered in the insolvency proceeding. The Reinsurer\'s liability shall be determined in accordance with the terms of this Treaty, including all applicable exclusions and limitations, regardless of the insolvency of the Company.

**11.2 Filing of Claims.** Any claim against the Reinsurer arising under this Treaty shall be filed by the liquidator, rehabilitator, receiver, conservator, or statutory successor of the Company within twenty-four (24) months of the date of the order of insolvency, rehabilitation, receivership, conservation, or similar order entered by the applicable court. Claims not filed by the liquidator, rehabilitator, receiver, conservator, or statutory successor of the Company within such twenty-four (24) month period shall be forever barred and the Reinsurer shall have no further liability with respect to any such claims. The filing of a claim within such twenty-four (24) month period shall be deemed sufficient to preserve the claim, even if the amount of the claim is not finally determined at the time of filing. The liquidator, rehabilitator, receiver, conservator, or statutory successor shall supplement the claim with additional information as it becomes available.

**11.3 Applicable Law.** This Article is intended to comply with the requirements of Ohio Revised Code § 3903.01 et seq. and the regulations of the Ohio Department of Insurance regarding insolvency clauses in reinsurance agreements. To the extent that any provision of this Article is inconsistent with the requirements of Ohio law or regulation, the requirements of Ohio law or regulation shall govern.

**11.4 Preference of Claims.** The Reinsurer\'s payment obligations under this Article shall be in accordance with, and subject to, any applicable priority scheme established by the insolvency court or under Ohio law. Nothing in this Treaty shall be construed to create any preference or priority in favor of the Reinsurer with respect to the assets of the Company\'s estate.

**[ARTICLE XII --- ACCESS TO RECORDS AND AUDIT]{.underline}**

**12.1 Audit Rights.** The Reinsurer, or its duly authorized representatives (including independent auditors and actuaries), shall have the right at any reasonable time during normal business hours to examine, audit, and inspect all books, records, documents, and accounts of the Company relating to business ceded under this Treaty, including but not limited to underwriting files, policy records, rating records, claim files, loss adjustment records, premium records, bordereaux, financial records, and such other information as may be relevant to the Reinsurer\'s rights and obligations under this Treaty. The Company shall make such records available at the Company\'s principal office in Columbus, Ohio, or at such other location as the parties may mutually agree.

**12.2 Notice of Audit.** The Reinsurer shall give the Company not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of its intention to conduct an audit or examination pursuant to this Article. The notice shall identify the scope and purpose of the audit and the estimated duration of the audit. The Company shall cooperate fully with the Reinsurer in the conduct of any audit, including by making available appropriate personnel to assist the Reinsurer\'s representatives.

**12.3 Duration of Access.** The rights provided in this Article shall survive the termination or expiration of this Treaty for a period of three (3) years following the later of: (a) the Expiration Date or the date of termination of this Treaty; or (b) the date on which all claims arising under Underlying Policies ceded under this Treaty have been finally settled or otherwise resolved.

**12.4 Costs.** The Reinsurer shall bear all costs and expenses of any audit conducted pursuant to this Article, including the fees and expenses of its auditors, actuaries, and other representatives. The Company shall bear its own internal costs of cooperating with the audit, including personnel time and document production costs.

**13.1 Term.** This Treaty shall be effective from January 1, 2024, at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Standard Time, through December 31, 2025, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Standard Time (the \"Treaty Period\"). The Treaty Period consists of two consecutive treaty years: (a) Treaty Year 1, from January 1, 2024 through December 31, 2024; and (b) Treaty Year 2, from January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025.

**13.2 Termination for Cause.** Either party may terminate this Treaty immediately upon written notice to the other party in the event of: (a) the insolvency, liquidation, or rehabilitation of the other party, or the appointment of a receiver, conservator, or similar official for the other party or for a substantial portion of the other party\'s assets; (b) a downgrade of the other party\'s A.M. This Article shall not be construed to excuse any willful or grossly negligent failure to comply with the terms and conditions of this Treaty.

**15.1 Intermediary.** Ridgeline Broking Ltd., with offices at 45 Lime Street, London EC3M 7AA (the \"Intermediary\"), is hereby recognized as the intermediary through which this Treaty was placed. The Intermediary has acted as reinsurance broker in connection with the negotiation and placement of this Treaty.

**15.2 Payments Through Intermediary.** All premium payments, loss payments, return premium payments, commission payments, reports, bordereaux, and other communications between the parties under this Treaty may be transmitted through the Intermediary, unless either party directs otherwise in writing. The parties agree that the Intermediary is authorized to receive and transmit such payments, reports, and communications on behalf of the parties.

**15.3 Intermediary as Agent of Reinsurer.** For purposes of premium and return premium, the Intermediary shall be deemed the agent of the Reinsurer. Payments of premium by the Company to the Intermediary shall constitute payment to the Reinsurer, and the Company shall be discharged of its premium obligation to the extent of such payment. For purposes of loss payments and loss adjustment expenses, the Intermediary shall be deemed the agent of the Company. Payments of losses by the Reinsurer to the Intermediary shall not constitute payment to the Company until such amounts are actually received by the Company. The Reinsurer shall remain liable for loss payments until such amounts are received by the Company.

**[ARTICLE XVI --- CURRENCY]{.underline}**

**16.1** All premiums, losses, loss adjustment expenses, commissions, and other amounts payable under this Treaty shall be expressed and settled in United States Dollars (USD). Where the original currency of any underlying transaction is other than United States Dollars, conversion shall be made at the rate of exchange prevailing on the date of the relevant transaction or, in the case of loss payments, on the date of the loss payment by the Company.

**[ARTICLE XVII --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**17.1** Each party shall maintain as confidential all information received from the other party in connection with this Treaty, including but not limited to the terms and conditions of this Treaty, financial information, underwriting data, claims information, and any other proprietary or sensitive information. Neither party shall disclose such information to any third party except as may be required by applicable law, regulation, court order, or regulatory directive, or as necessary for the administration of this Treaty (including disclosure to auditors, regulators, retrocessionaires, rating agencies, legal counsel, actuaries, and other professional advisors retained by either party in connection with this Treaty), provided that any such third-party recipient is bound by obligations of confidentiality substantially similar to those set forth herein. This confidentiality obligation shall survive the termination or expiration of this Treaty for a period of three (3) years.

**[ARTICLE XX --- ENTIRE AGREEMENT; AMENDMENTS]{.underline}**

**20.1 Entire Agreement.** This Treaty, together with any addenda, endorsements, schedules, or amendments executed by both parties, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, warranties, commitments, offers, contracts, and understandings of any kind, whether written or oral, relating to the subject matter hereof. **20.3 Severability.** If any provision of this Treaty is held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by any court, tribunal, or arbitral body of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions of this Treaty shall continue in full force and effect, and the invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision shall be deemed modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, legal, and enforceable, consistent with the original intent of the parties.

102	
103	**[A. Coverage A --- Building]{.underline}**
104	
105	Subject to the Limit of Insurance stated on the Declarations Page for Coverage A, and subject to all terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations of this Policy, the Insurer agrees to pay for direct physical loss of or damage to the building at the Described Premises caused by or resulting from a Covered Cause of Loss.
106	
107	For purposes of this Coverage A, the term \"building\" means and includes the following:
108	
109	1\. The building structure located at the Described Premises, including all completed additions thereto, whether completed prior to or during the Policy Period;
110	
111	2\. Fixtures permanently installed in or on the building, including but not limited to built-in cabinetry, countertops, shelving, and similar items that are permanently affixed to the building structure;
112	
113	3\. Machinery and equipment used for the service, maintenance, and operation of the building, including but not limited to: heating, ventilating, and air conditioning systems (HVAC); fire protection and suppression systems (including sprinkler systems, fire alarms, and fire detection equipment); plumbing systems; electrical wiring, panels, and distribution systems; elevators, escalators, and hoisting apparatus; boilers and pressure vessels used for building service; and security systems;
114	
115	4\. Cold-storage compressor units, refrigeration systems (including ammonia-based refrigeration compressors, condensers, evaporators, piping, and controls), loading dock apparatus (including hydraulic dock levelers, dock seals, and dock shelters), conveyor systems (including belt conveyors, roller conveyors, and sortation systems), and all structural components integral to the operation of the distribution and cold-storage facility;
116	
117	5\. Outdoor fixtures, including but not limited to light poles, fencing, signage permanently affixed to the building or grounds, retaining walls, and paved surfaces forming part of the building\'s operational infrastructure;
118	
119	6\. Personal property owned by the Named Insured that is used to maintain or service the building or its premises, including fire extinguishing equipment, outdoor furniture, floor coverings, and appliances used for refrigerating, ventilating, cooking, dishwashing, or laundering; and
120	
121	7\. All additions, alterations, and improvements to the building made during the Policy Period with the knowledge or consent of the Named Insured, provided such additions, alterations, or improvements become part of the building structure.
122	
123	**Coverage A does NOT include the following:**
124	
125	> • Land (including the land on which the building is located), water, growing crops, lawns, or standing timber;
126	>
127	> • The cost of excavations, underground flues, underground pipes, underground wiring, underground drains, grading, backfilling, or filling;
128	>
129	> • Foundations of the building that are below the lowest basement floor, or if there is no basement, foundations that are below the surface of the ground inside the foundation walls;
130	>
131	> • Underground pipes, flues, drains, or wiring that are located below the surface of the ground and outside the foundation walls of the building; and
132	>
133	> • Piers, wharves, or docks.
134	
135	The Limit of Insurance for Coverage A is \$52,000,000 as stated on the Declarations Page.
136	
137	**[B. Coverage B --- Business Personal Property]{.underline}**
138	
139	Subject to the Limit of Insurance stated on the Declarations Page for Coverage B, and subject to all terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations of this Policy, the Insurer agrees to pay for direct physical loss of or damage to business personal property caused by or resulting from a Covered Cause of Loss.
140	
141	For purposes of this Coverage B, \"business personal property\" means and includes the following categories of property, unless such property is more specifically described under Coverage A --- Building:
142	
143	1\. **Furniture and Fixtures:** All furniture, fixtures, and fittings owned by the Named Insured and located in or on the building at the Described Premises, including office furniture, workstations, shelving not permanently affixed to the building, portable partitions, and similar items used in the conduct of the Named Insured\'s business;
144	
145	2\. **Machinery and Equipment:** Machinery and equipment owned by the Named Insured that is not covered under Coverage A, including warehouse management system hardware, barcode scanners, portable material handling equipment (forklifts, pallet jacks, hand trucks), portable refrigeration monitoring devices, packaging equipment, and similar items;
146	
147	3\. **Stock:** Goods held by the Named Insured for storage, distribution, sale, or in the process of being manufactured, packaged, or prepared for shipment, including perishable goods stored in the cold-storage facility, dry goods held in the ambient distribution areas, and goods held on consignment or bailment by the Named Insured;
148	
149	4\. **All Other Personal Property:** All other tangible personal property owned by the Named Insured and used in the Named Insured\'s business, including but not limited to: tenant\'s improvements and betterments (if the Named Insured is a tenant), leased personal property for which the Named Insured is contractually responsible, patterns, dies, molds, drawings, and similar items; and
150	
151	5\. **Personal Property of Others:** Personal property of others that is in the Named Insured\'s care, custody, or control, including goods held for customers awaiting distribution, storage, or shipment. Coverage for personal property of others is limited to the Named Insured\'s legal liability for such property, unless broader coverage is required by a written contract between the Named Insured and the property owner.
152	
153	**Territorial Extension for Business Personal Property.** Coverage B also applies to business personal property owned by the Named Insured while temporarily located at any location within the continental United States, provided that such property is: (a) in transit to or from the Described Premises in the ordinary course of the Named Insured\'s warehousing and distribution business, or (b) temporarily stored at such other location in the ordinary course of the Named Insured\'s business. This territorial extension is subject to a sublimit of Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) at any single off-premises location. The Named Insured shall maintain adequate records of property at off-premises locations and shall provide such records to the Insurer upon request.
154	
155	**Coverage B does NOT include the following:**
156	
157	> • Accounts, bills, currency, food stamps, other evidences of debt, money, notes, or securities (except as provided under a separate crime or fidelity policy);
158	>
159	> • Animals, unless owned by others and held in the Named Insured\'s care, custody, or control;
160	>
161	> • Automobiles held for sale (which are addressed under separate auto coverage);
162	>
163	> • Bridges, roadways, walks, patios, or other paved surfaces; and
164	>
165	> • The cost of research, development, or other expenses incurred in recreating lost data or records.
166	
167	The Limit of Insurance for Coverage B is \$28,000,000 as stated on the Declarations Page, subject to the off-premises sublimit stated above.
168	
169	**[C. Coverage C --- Business Interruption / Loss of Income]{.underline}**
170	
171	Subject to the Limit of Insurance stated on the Declarations Page for Coverage C, and subject to all terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations of this Policy, the Insurer agrees to pay for the actual loss of Business Income that the Named Insured sustains due to the necessary suspension of the Named Insured\'s operations during the Period of Restoration.
172	
173	**Suspension of Operations.** For purposes of this Coverage C, \"suspension\" means: (a) the slowdown or cessation of the Named Insured\'s business activities; or (b) that a part or all of the Described Premises is rendered untenantable as a result of direct physical loss of or damage to Covered Property at the Described Premises caused by or resulting from a Covered Cause of Loss.
174	
175	**Business Income.** As more fully defined in Section VI of this Policy, \"Business Income\" means: (i) the net income (net profit or loss before income taxes) that would have been earned or incurred by the Named Insured had no direct physical loss or damage occurred; and (ii) continuing normal operating expenses incurred by the Named Insured, including payroll. For the avoidance of doubt, Business Income does not include any income that would not have been earned had the loss or damage not occurred, and the Named Insured bears the burden of establishing the amount of Business Income that would have been earned during the Period of Restoration.
176	
177	**Period of Restoration.** As more fully defined in Section VI of this Policy, the \"Period of Restoration\" begins seventy-two (72) hours after the time of direct physical loss or damage caused by a Covered Cause of Loss at the Described Premises, and ends on the earlier of: (a) the date when the Covered Property at the Described Premises should be repaired, rebuilt, or replaced with reasonable speed and similar quality; or (b) twelve (12) months from the date of direct physical loss or damage. The twelve-month outer limit reflects the parties\' agreed maximum indemnity period for business interruption losses under this Policy. The Period of Restoration does not include any increased period required due to the enforcement of any ordinance or law regulating the construction or repair of damaged buildings; such additional period is addressed separately under the Ordinance or Law Additional Coverage set forth in Section II.B of this Policy.
178	
179	**Extended Business Income.** In addition to the coverage provided above, this Policy covers the reduction in Business Income that continues after the Period of Restoration has ended, for an additional period not to exceed sixty (60) days following the end of the Period of Restoration. This Extended Business Income coverage recognizes that the Named Insured may require additional time to rebuild its customer base and restore operations to pre-loss levels following completion of repairs or replacement. The Extended Business Income coverage is subject to the overall Limit of Insurance of Eighteen Million Dollars (\$18,000,000) stated on the Declarations Page for Coverage C, and no additional limit is provided for the extended period.
180	
181	**Civil Authority Coverage.** This Coverage C also covers the actual loss of Business Income sustained by the Named Insured caused by action of a civil authority that prohibits access to the Described Premises, provided that: (a) such action is taken in response to dangerous physical conditions resulting from direct physical loss of or damage to property other than the Described Premises; and (b) access to the Described Premises is prohibited by the civil authority as a direct result of such physical conditions. Civil Authority coverage begins seventy-two (72) hours after the time the civil authority issues the order prohibiting access and continues for a period not to exceed thirty (30) consecutive days from the date of the civil authority\'s order. Civil Authority coverage is subject to the overall Limit of Insurance stated on the Declarations Page for Coverage C.
182	
183	**Waiting Period.** No coverage shall be afforded under this Coverage C for Business Income losses sustained during the first seventy-two (72) hours following the time of direct physical loss or damage. This seventy-two-hour waiting period applies separately to each occurrence and constitutes a condition precedent to the Insurer\'s obligation to pay Business Income losses.
184	
185	**Limit of Insurance.** The Limit of Insurance for Coverage C --- Business Interruption / Loss of Income is Eighteen Million Dollars (\$18,000,000), which represents the maximum amount payable under this Coverage C for any single occurrence, including Extended Business Income and Civil Authority coverage, during the twelve (12) month indemnity period.
186	
187	**[SECTION II --- ADDITIONAL COVERAGES]{.underline}**
188	
189	**[A. Debris Removal]{.underline}**
190	
191	The Insurer will pay the Named Insured\'s reasonable and necessary expense to remove debris of Covered Property caused by or resulting from a Covered Cause of Loss that occurs during the Policy Period. Debris removal expense includes the cost of removing from the Described Premises any remains of Covered Property that has been damaged or destroyed by a Covered Cause of Loss, including the cost of transporting such debris to an appropriate disposal site.
192	
193	The amount payable under this Additional Coverage for debris removal shall be an additional amount equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of the amount of covered direct physical loss or damage to Covered Property at the Described Premises, but in no event shall the total amount payable for debris removal under this provision exceed Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000) per occurrence. This Two Million Dollar cap applies regardless of the amount of covered direct physical loss or damage sustained. If the Named Insured\'s actual debris removal expense exceeds the lesser of (i) twenty-five percent (25%) of the covered direct physical loss amount, or (ii) Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000) per occurrence, the Named Insured shall bear the excess cost without contribution from the Insurer.
194	
195	Debris removal expense covered under this provision does not include: (a) costs to extract \"pollutants\" from land or water; (b) costs to remove, restore, or replace polluted land or water; or (c) costs associated with the cleanup or removal of hazardous materials, asbestos, or other regulated substances, which costs are addressed separately under the Pollution Cleanup Additional Coverage set forth in Section II.C of this Policy.
196	
197	The debris removal coverage provided under this Section II.A is payable in addition to the applicable Limit of Insurance under Coverage A or Coverage B. Amounts payable for debris removal shall not reduce the amounts otherwise payable under Coverage A or Coverage B of this Policy. The debris removal coverage constitutes an additional coverage amount over and above the Coverage A and Coverage B limits stated on the Declarations Page.
198	
199	The Named Insured shall use reasonable efforts to minimize debris removal costs, including obtaining competitive bids for debris removal services when practicable under the circumstances. The Insurer reserves the right to approve debris removal contractors and to participate in the selection of disposal sites, provided that such approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
200	
201	**[B. Ordinance or Law Coverage]{.underline}**
202	
203	The Insurer will pay for loss or additional costs the Named Insured is required to incur because of the enforcement of any ordinance or law that: (i) requires the demolition of undamaged portions of the building at the Described Premises; (ii) regulates the construction, repair, or restoration of damaged buildings; or (iii) requires the testing, removal, cleanup, abatement, or other remediation of building materials made necessary by the enforcement of building codes, fire codes, safety regulations, or similar governmental requirements.
204	
205	This Ordinance or Law coverage includes three subcoverages:
206	
207	**Subcoverage 1 --- Loss in Value of Undamaged Portion.** If a Covered Cause of Loss results in damage to the building at the Described Premises, and an ordinance or law requires the demolition of the undamaged portion of the building, the Insurer will pay for the loss in value of the undamaged portion of the building. The loss in value shall be determined as the difference between the value of the undamaged portion of the building before the enforcement of the ordinance or law and the value of the undamaged portion after enforcement (taking into account the required demolition).
208	
209	**Subcoverage 2 --- Demolition Cost.** If a Covered Cause of Loss results in damage to the building at the Described Premises, and an ordinance or law requires the demolition of the undamaged portion of the building, the Insurer will pay the reasonable and necessary cost of demolishing the undamaged portion of the building and clearing the site of the resulting debris.
210	
211	**Subcoverage 3 --- Increased Cost of Construction.** If a Covered Cause of Loss results in damage to the building at the Described Premises, and an ordinance or law requires that the building be repaired, rebuilt, or replaced in a manner that increases the cost of construction beyond what would be required absent such ordinance or law, the Insurer will pay the increased cost of construction necessary to comply with the requirements of such ordinance or law.
212	
213	The combined total payable under all three subcoverages of this Ordinance or Law Additional Coverage shall not exceed Four Million Dollars (\$4,000,000) per occurrence. This sublimit is in addition to the Coverage A Limit of Insurance for direct physical loss or damage to the building, but is subject to the Combined Policy Limit stated on the Declarations Page.
214	
215	This coverage applies to the enforcement of any ordinance or law that is in force at the time of loss, including building codes, zoning ordinances, and land use regulations enacted by any governmental authority having jurisdiction over the Described Premises. This coverage does not apply to costs associated with pollutant cleanup required by environmental law or regulation, which costs are addressed separately under the Pollution Cleanup Additional Coverage set forth in Section II.C of this Policy.
216	
217	The Named Insured must begin actual repair, rebuilding, or replacement of the damaged building as soon as reasonably possible after the loss, and must notify the Insurer of any ordinance or law enforcement that may affect the cost or scope of repair or replacement.
218	
219	**[C. Pollution Cleanup]{.underline}**
220	
221	The Insurer will pay the Named Insured\'s reasonable and necessary expense to extract, remove, contain, treat, detoxify, neutralize, or dispose of \"pollutants\" from land or water at the Described Premises, if the release, discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, or escape of such pollutants is caused by or results from a Covered Cause of Loss that occurs during the Policy Period.
222	
223	The amount payable under this Pollution Cleanup Additional Coverage shall not exceed Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per occurrence. This sublimit applies regardless of the total cost of pollution cleanup, and any cleanup expenses in excess of this sublimit shall be borne solely by the Named Insured.
224	
225	This Pollution Cleanup coverage applies only to \"pollutants\" (as defined in Section VI of this Policy) that are released, discharged, dispersed, or that seep, migrate, or escape as a direct result of a Covered Cause of Loss, and only if such release, discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, or escape constitutes a \"Sudden and Accidental Discharge\" as that term is defined in Section VI (Definitions) of this Policy. The requirement that the pollution event qualify as a Sudden and Accidental Discharge is a condition precedent to the Insurer\'s obligation to pay under this Pollution Cleanup Additional Coverage.
226	
227	The Named Insured must report the pollution event to the Insurer as soon as practicable and must commence cleanup operations within one hundred eighty (180) days of the date of the Covered Cause of Loss that gave rise to the pollution event. Failure to commence cleanup within this 180-day period shall relieve the Insurer of its obligation to pay under this Additional Coverage, unless the Named Insured demonstrates that the delay was caused by governmental order or other circumstances beyond the Named Insured\'s reasonable control.
228	
229	**[D. Equipment Breakdown]{.underline}**
230	
231	The Insurer will pay for direct physical loss of or damage to Covered Property caused by an equipment breakdown, including the failure of electrical, mechanical, and pressure equipment located at the Described Premises. For purposes of this Additional Coverage, \"equipment breakdown\" means the sudden and accidental breakdown of equipment that causes physical damage to the equipment, necessitating its repair or replacement. Equipment breakdown includes, but is not limited to, mechanical failure, electrical arcing, motor burnout, compressor failure, rupture or bursting of pressure vessels, and similar failures of operating equipment.
232	
233	The amount payable under this Equipment Breakdown Additional Coverage shall not exceed Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) per occurrence. This sublimit is in addition to any amounts payable under Coverage A for direct physical loss of or damage to the building.
234	
235	This coverage includes the cost of spoilage of perishable goods stored in the cold-storage facility resulting from equipment breakdown, including loss due to ammonia leakage or contamination caused by the failure of refrigeration compressors or related equipment. The Named Insured shall take all reasonable measures to preserve perishable goods following an equipment breakdown, including arranging for temporary cold-storage facilities where practicable.
236	
237	This Equipment Breakdown Additional Coverage does not apply to loss or damage caused by: (a) gradual deterioration, wear and tear, or depletion; (b) rust, corrosion, erosion, or settling; (c) damage that is the direct result of scheduled or routine maintenance or testing; or (d) any equipment that has been removed from service and is not being maintained in operable condition.
238	
239	A separate deductible of Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$50,000) per equipment breakdown occurrence applies to claims under this Additional Coverage, which deductible is in lieu of (and not in addition to) the per-occurrence deductible stated on the Declarations Page.
240	
241	**[E. Fire Department Service Charge]{.underline}**
242	
243	The Insurer will pay up to Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$50,000) for fire department service charges assumed by contract or agreement by the Named Insured, or for which the Named Insured is otherwise legally obligated, when the fire department is called to protect Covered Property from a Covered Cause of Loss. This amount is payable in addition to the applicable limits of insurance and shall not reduce any other coverage amounts under this Policy. No deductible applies to this Additional Coverage.
244	
245	**[F. Preservation of Property]{.underline}**
246	
247	If it is necessary to move Covered Property from the Described Premises to preserve it from an actual or imminent Covered Cause of Loss, the Insurer will pay for any direct physical loss of or damage to such Covered Property while it is being moved or while temporarily stored at another location. This coverage applies for a period not to exceed sixty (60) days at the temporary location, commencing on the date the property is first moved from the Described Premises. Coverage under this provision is subject to the applicable Coverage A or Coverage B Limit of Insurance and does not provide any additional limit.
248	
249	**[SECTION III --- SUE AND LABOR]{.underline}**
250	
251	In case of actual or imminent loss or damage to Covered Property from a Covered Cause of Loss, the Named Insured shall use all reasonable means to protect, preserve, and safeguard the Covered Property from further loss or damage, and any reasonable and necessary expenses incurred by the Named Insured for such purpose shall be reimbursed by the Insurer.
252	
253	Sue-and-labor expenses payable under this Section III are payable in addition to the applicable Limits of Insurance stated on the Declarations Page. Amounts reimbursed by the Insurer under this Sue and Labor provision shall not reduce the amounts otherwise payable under any Coverage of this Policy, including but not limited to Coverage A --- Building, Coverage B --- Business Personal Property, and Coverage C --- Business Interruption / Loss of Income. The Insurer\'s obligation to reimburse sue-and-labor expenses is separate from and in addition to its obligation to indemnify the Named Insured for covered direct physical loss or damage.
254	
255	The Named Insured\'s duty to protect Covered Property from further loss or damage arises immediately upon the Named Insured becoming aware of actual or imminent loss or damage, whether or not the Insurer has been notified of the loss at that time. This duty applies regardless of whether the loss is ultimately determined to be covered under this Policy. The Named Insured\'s compliance with the duty to mitigate shall not be construed as an admission of coverage or liability by the Insurer.
256	
257	Reimbursement under this Sue and Labor provision shall include, without limitation, the following categories of expenses when reasonably and necessarily incurred to minimize or prevent further loss to Covered Property:
258	
259	> \(a\) Costs of temporary repairs to the building or building systems to prevent further deterioration or damage;
260	>
261	> \(b\) Emerg
