21	**[SECTION IV --- COVERED CAUSES OF LOSS (SPECIAL FORM)]{.underline}**
22	
23	**[A. Covered Causes of Loss]{.underline}**
24	
25	This Policy is written on a Special Form (All-Risk) basis. Accordingly, this Policy covers risks of direct physical loss or damage to Covered Property from any cause, unless the loss is excluded under Section V (Exclusions) of this Policy or limited under any other provision of this Policy.
26	
27	Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, and for purposes of illustration, Covered Causes of Loss under this Policy include, but are not limited to, the following: fire; lightning; windstorm; hail; explosion; smoke; riot and civil commotion; vandalism; sprinkler leakage; sinkhole collapse; volcanic action; theft; falling objects; weight of snow, ice, or sleet; water damage (including damage caused by burst pipes, leaking appliances, or accidental discharge of water from fire protective systems); collapse of buildings or structures; vehicle impact; aircraft impact; and all other risks of direct physical loss or damage not specifically excluded or limited under this Policy.
28	
29	**Flood.** Flood is a Covered Cause of Loss under this Policy, subject to the annual aggregate sublimit of Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) as stated on the Declarations Page and the specific flood loss conditions set forth in Section IX of this Policy. The inclusion of flood as a Covered Cause of Loss is subject to the additional flood deductible and other conditions specified in Section IX.
30	
31	**Earthquake.** Earthquake is a Covered Cause of Loss under this Policy, subject to the annual aggregate sublimit of Three Million Dollars (\$3,000,000) as stated on the Declarations Page and the specific earthquake loss conditions set forth in Section IX of this Policy. The inclusion of earthquake as a Covered Cause of Loss is subject to the additional earthquake deductible and other conditions specified in Section IX.
32	
33	The determination of whether a particular cause of loss is a Covered Cause of Loss under this Policy shall be made without regard to any other policy of insurance. The burden of proving that a loss resulted from an excluded cause of loss rests with the Insurer.
34	
35	**[B. Flood Coverage Provisions]{.underline}**
36	
37	For purposes of this Policy, \"Flood\" means: (a) the overflow of inland or tidal waters; (b) the unusual and rapid accumulation or runoff of surface waters from any source; (c) mudflow, meaning a river of liquid and flowing mud on the surfaces of normally dry land areas, as when earth is carried by a current of water; and (d) collapse or subsidence of land along the shore of a lake or similar body of water as a result of erosion or undermining caused by waves or currents of water exceeding anticipated cyclical levels that result in a flood as defined above.
38	
39	Flood is covered under this Policy subject to the following conditions and limitations:
40	
41	1\. **Annual Aggregate Sublimit.** The maximum amount payable for all flood losses occurring during the Policy Period shall not exceed Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) in the annual aggregate. Once the annual aggregate sublimit has been exhausted by payment of flood losses during the Policy Period, no further flood losses shall be covered under this Policy for the remainder of the Policy Period.
42	
43	2\. **Flood Waiting Period.** No coverage shall be afforded under this Flood Coverage provision for losses occurring during the first seventy-two (72) hours from the commencement of any flood event. This waiting period applies separately to each flood occurrence.
44	
45	3\. **Flood Deductible.** In addition to the per-occurrence Deductible stated on the Declarations Page, a separate flood deductible of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per flood occurrence shall apply to all claims under this Flood Coverage provision. The flood deductible shall be applied after application of the standard per-occurrence Deductible.
46	
47	4\. **Compliance with NFIP.** The Named Insured shall comply with all applicable requirements of the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and shall maintain any NFIP policy required by law or by any applicable mortgage or loan agreement.
48	
49	**[C. Earthquake Coverage Provisions]{.underline}**
50	
51	For purposes of this Policy, \"Earthquake\" means the shaking or trembling of the earth caused by tectonic or volcanic forces, including but not limited to: earth sinking, rising, or shifting; landslide or mudslide caused directly by earthquake; and aftershocks or secondary tremors arising from the same seismic event. Earthquake does not include tidal wave or tsunami, volcanic eruption (other than earthquake tremors caused by volcanic activity), or land subsidence not related to seismic activity.
52	
53	Earthquake is covered under this Policy subject to the following conditions and limitations:
54	
55	1\. **Annual Aggregate Sublimit.** The maximum amount payable for all earthquake losses occurring during the Policy Period shall not exceed Three Million Dollars (\$3,000,000) in the annual aggregate. Once the annual aggregate sublimit has been exhausted by payment of earthquake losses during the Policy Period, no further earthquake losses shall be covered under this Policy for the remainder of the Policy Period.
56	
57	2\. **Single Occurrence.** All earthquake shocks occurring within any continuous period of one hundred sixty-eight hours (168 hours or seven days) shall constitute a single earthquake occurrence for purposes of applying the earthquake deductible and the annual aggregate sublimit.
58	
59	3\. **Earthquake Deductible.** In addition to the per-occurrence Deductible stated on the Declarations Page, a separate earthquake deductible shall apply to each earthquake occurrence. The earthquake deductible shall be equal to two percent (2%) of the applicable Coverage A or Coverage B Limit of Insurance, subject to a minimum earthquake deductible of Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$250,000) per earthquake occurrence.
60	
61	4\. **Application to Described Premises Only.** Earthquake coverage applies only to Covered Property located at the Described Premises and does not extend to property at off-premises locations under the territorial extension provisions of Coverage B or Section VIII.
62	
63	**[SECTION V --- EXCLUSIONS]{.underline}**
64	
65	**[A. Exclusions Applicable to All Coverages]{.underline}**
66	
67	The following causes of loss and resulting loss or damage are excluded from coverage under this Policy. These exclusions apply to all coverages provided under this Policy, including Coverage A --- Building, Coverage B --- Business Personal Property, Coverage C --- Business Interruption / Loss of Income, and all Additional Coverages set forth in Section II, unless a specific Additional Coverage expressly provides otherwise.
68	
69	**1. War and Military Action.** Any hostile or warlike action in time of peace or war, including action in hindering, combating, or defending against an actual, impending, or expected attack: (a) by any government or sovereign power (de jure or de facto), or by any authority maintaining or using military, naval, or air forces; (b) by military, naval, or air forces; or (c) by an agent of any such government, power, authority, or forces. This exclusion also applies to insurrection, rebellion, revolution, civil war, usurped power, or any action taken by governmental authority in hindering, combating, or defending against any of the foregoing. For the avoidance of doubt, this exclusion applies solely to war-related and military-related governmental actions and does not extend to governmental actions taken pursuant to building codes, zoning ordinances, environmental regulations, or similar civil regulatory authority.
70	
71	**2. Nuclear Hazard.** Nuclear reaction, nuclear radiation, or radioactive contamination, however caused, including any self-sustaining process of nuclear fission. This exclusion applies whether or not the nuclear hazard results from a Covered Cause of Loss. However, if fire ensues from nuclear reaction, nuclear radiation, or radioactive contamination, the Insurer will pay for the loss or damage caused by the ensuing fire.
72	
73	**3. Governmental Action (Limited).** Seizure, confiscation, nationalization, or destruction of property by order of any governmental authority. However, this exclusion does not apply to: (a) destruction of property ordered by a governmental authority to prevent the spread of fire (fire-line demolition), provided the fire constitutes a Covered Cause of Loss; and (b) loss of Business Income caused by action of a civil authority that prohibits access to the Described Premises, as covered under the Civil Authority provision of Coverage C. This exclusion is intended to apply to governmental seizure, confiscation, or destruction of property in the exercise of sovereign power, and shall not be construed to exclude coverage for loss or damage resulting from the enforcement of building codes, zoning ordinances, fire codes, safety regulations, or similar civil regulatory requirements, which are addressed under the Ordinance or Law Additional Coverage set forth in Section II.B of this Policy.
74	
75	**4. Intentional Loss.** Any dishonest, fraudulent, or criminal act committed by or at the direction of the Named Insured or any partner, member, officer, manager, director, employee, or authorized agent of the Named Insured, whether acting alone or in collusion with others. This exclusion applies to the Named Insured\'s interest in all Covered Property, regardless of whether the Named Insured participated in or had knowledge of the act.
76	
77	**5. Wear and Tear / Gradual Deterioration.** Loss or damage caused by or resulting from any of the following: wear and tear; inherent vice; latent defect; mechanical breakdown (except as covered under the Equipment Breakdown Additional Coverage set forth in Section II.D); rust; corrosion; decay; deterioration; smog; settling, cracking, shrinking, bulging, or expansion of foundations, walls, floors, ceilings, or roofs; nesting or infestation by insects, birds, rodents, or other animals; or marring or scratching. However, if a Covered Cause of Loss ensues from any of the foregoing, the Insurer will pay for the loss or damage caused by the ensuing Covered Cause of Loss.
78	
79	**6. Cyber / Electronic Risk.** Loss or damage caused by or resulting from: (a) unauthorized access to or use of any computer system, whether owned by the Named Insured or by any other party; (b) introduction of malicious code, including viruses, worms, trojan horses, ransomware, or similar code, into any computer system; (c) denial of service attack or other interruption of computer network availability; (d) hacking, phishing, or other cyber-attack; or (e) loss of, damage to, or corruption of electronic data, regardless of any other cause or event that contributes concurrently or in any sequence to the loss. This exclusion does not apply to ensuing physical damage to Covered Property (other than electronic data) that results from a computer-related incident, if such ensuing physical damage would otherwise be covered under this Policy.
80	
81	**7. Voluntary Parting.** Voluntary parting with any property by the Named Insured or anyone else to whom the property has been entrusted, if induced to do so by any fraudulent scheme, trick, device, or false pretense.
82	
83	**8. Infidelity / Employee Dishonesty.** Loss or damage caused by or resulting from dishonest or criminal acts committed by employees of the Named Insured, whether acting alone or in collusion with other persons. Such losses are addressed under separate fidelity or crime coverage and are not covered under this Policy.
84	
85	**9. Consequential Loss.** Delay, loss of use, or loss of market, except as specifically provided under Coverage C --- Business Interruption / Loss of Income. This Policy does not cover indirect or consequential damages of any kind except to the extent that Business Income coverage is expressly provided under Coverage C.
86	
87	**The following perils are expressly NOT excluded under this Policy and are covered subject to the applicable sublimits, deductibles, and conditions stated herein:**
88	
89	> • **Flood** --- Covered subject to the annual aggregate sublimit of \$5,000,000 and the conditions stated in Section IV.B and Section IX of this Policy.
90	>
91	> • **Earthquake** --- Covered subject to the annual aggregate sublimit of \$3,000,000 and the conditions stated in Section IV.C and Section IX of this Policy.
92	>
93	> • **Terrorism** --- Covered under this Policy. This Policy provides coverage for certified acts of terrorism as defined in the Terrorism Risk Insurance Act of 2002 (TRIA), as amended. The Named Insured\'s election to maintain terrorism coverage is confirmed by Endorsement No. 3 attached hereto.
94	>
95	> • **Sudden and Accidental Pollution** --- Covered subject to the \$500,000 per occurrence sublimit under the Pollution Cleanup Additional Coverage stated in Section II.C, and subject to the requirement that the pollution event constitute a \"Sudden and Accidental Discharge\" as defined in Section VI of this Policy.
96	
97	**[B. Pollution Exclusion and Carve-Back]{.underline}**
98	
99	**Pollution Exclusion.** The Insurer shall not be liable for loss or damage caused by or resulting from the discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release, or escape of \"pollutants,\" regardless of any other cause or event that contributes concurrently or in any sequence to the loss, unless such discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release, or escape constitutes a Sudden and Accidental Discharge as defined in Section VI of this Policy.
100	
101	For purposes of this exclusion, \"pollutants\" means any solid, liquid, gaseous, or thermal irritant or contaminant, including but not limited to smoke, vapor, soot, fumes, acids, alkalis, chemicals, refrigerants (including but not limited to ammonia and Freon), waste materials (including recycled, reconditioned, or reclaimed materials), and all materials listed as hazardous substances or toxic pollutants under any applicable federal, state, or local environmental law, statute, or regulation, including the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA), the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), and the Ohio Environmental Protection Act.
102	
103	**Carve-Back for Sudden and Accidental Discharge.** Notwithstanding the Pollution Exclusion stated above, this Policy provides affirmative coverage for pollution cleanup expenses when the release, discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, or escape of pollutants constitutes a \"Sudden and Accidental Discharge\" as that term is defined in Section VI (Definitions) of this Policy. Such coverage is subject to the sublimit of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per occurrence stated under the Pollution Cleanup Additional Coverage in Section II.C of this Policy.
104	
105	The Named Insured bears the burden of establishing that a particular pollution event qualifies as a Sudden and Accidental Discharge under the three-part definition set forth in Section VI. The detailed definition of \"Sudden and Accidental Discharge\" contained in Section VI of this Policy governs the scope and application of this carve-back and shall be construed in accordance with its plain language.
106	
107	This Pollution Exclusion does not apply to damage caused by smoke, soot, or fumes from a hostile fire, which damage is covered as a direct result of the fire peril without reference to this exclusion.
108	
109	**[SECTION VI --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**
110	
111	The following terms, when capitalized and used in this Policy (including the Declarations Page, all Sections, all Additional Coverages, all Endorsements, and all other documents forming part of this Policy), shall have the meanings set forth below. Terms not defined in this Section shall have their plain and ordinary meaning under the laws of the State of Ohio.
112	
113	**1. \"Covered Cause of Loss\"** --- A cause of direct physical loss or damage to Covered Property that is not excluded or limited under Section V (Exclusions) of this Policy or under any other provision, condition, or limitation contained in this Policy. The determination of whether a cause of loss constitutes a Covered Cause of Loss shall be made without reference to any other policy of insurance maintained by the Named Insured. Under the Special Form (All-Risk) basis of this Policy, all causes of direct physical loss or damage are Covered Causes of Loss unless specifically excluded or limited.
114	
115	**2. \"Covered Property\"** --- The building, business personal property, and other property described in Section I of this Policy, including any property covered under the Additional Coverages set forth in Section II. Covered Property includes property at the Described Premises and, to the extent provided in Coverage B and Section VIII, property at off-premises locations within the continental United States.
116	
117	**3. \"Named Insured\"** --- Summit Ridge Warehousing LLC, an Ohio limited liability company, and its successors and assigns as may be approved in writing by the Insurer in accordance with Section VII.K of this Policy.
118	
119	**4. \"Occurrence\"** --- Any one accident, event, or series of related accidents or events arising from one cause. For purposes of applying the per-occurrence Deductible stated on the Declarations Page and any per-occurrence sublimit stated in this Policy, all loss or damage arising from one cause shall be deemed to constitute a single occurrence, regardless of the number of locations, claimants, or claims involved, and regardless of the period of time over which the loss or damage develops or manifests, provided that all such loss or damage is attributable to a single originating cause. For the avoidance of doubt, two or more losses that arise from independent and unrelated causes shall constitute separate occurrences, even if they occur simultaneously or within a short period of time. The determination of whether multiple losses constitute a single occurrence or multiple occurrences shall be made by reference to the \"cause\" of the loss, and not by reference to the \"effect\" or the time period during which effects are manifested.
120	
121	**5. \"Period of Restoration\"** --- The period of time that:
122	
123	> \(a\) begins seventy-two (72) hours after the time of direct physical loss or damage caused by a Covered Cause of Loss at the Described Premises; and
124	>
125	> \(b\) ends on the earlier of:
126	>
127	> \(i\) the date when the Covered Property at the Described Premises should be repaired, rebuilt, or replaced with reasonable speed and similar quality; or
128	>
129	> \(ii\) twelve (12) months from the date of direct physical loss or damage.
130	
131	The Period of Restoration does not include any increased period required due to the enforcement of any ordinance or law regulating the construction, repair, or restoration of damaged buildings; such additional period, if any, is addressed under the Ordinance or Law Additional Coverage set forth in Section II.B of this Policy. The phrase \"with reasonable speed and similar quality\" means the time that would reasonably be required by a competent contractor, working diligently and without unnecessary delay, to repair, rebuild, or replace the damaged Covered Property using materials and methods of comparable quality and suitability to those that existed prior to the loss, taking into account the availability of materials, labor, and permits at the time of loss.
132	
133	**6. \"Pollutants\"** --- Any solid, liquid, gaseous, or thermal irritant or contaminant, including but not limited to smoke, vapor, soot, fumes, acids, alkalis, chemicals, refrigerants (including ammonia, Freon, and similar substances used in cold-storage and refrigeration systems), waste materials (including materials intended for recycling, reconditioning, or reclamation), and all materials listed as hazardous substances or toxic pollutants under any applicable federal, state, or local environmental law, statute, regulation, or ordinance. The term \"pollutants\" also includes any substance that, when released into the environment, is capable of causing bodily injury, property damage, or environmental contamination, regardless of whether such substance is listed under any specific statutory or regulatory scheme.
134	
135	**7. \"Sudden and Accidental Discharge\"** --- A discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release, or escape of pollutants that meets all of the following criteria:
136	
137	> \(a\) the discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release, or escape is not expected or intended by the Named Insured;
138	>
139	> \(b\) the discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release, or escape takes place in its entirety at a specific time and place during the Policy Period; and
140	>
141	> \(c\) the discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release, or escape results directly from a sudden, identifiable, and accidental event.
142	
143	For purposes of this definition, \"sudden\" means abrupt and not gradual. A discharge or release that occurs slowly, incrementally, or over a prolonged period of time does not qualify as \"sudden\" regardless of whether it was unexpected by the Named Insured. The phrase \"at a specific time and place\" means that the entire discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release, or escape can be attributed to a discrete incident commencing at an identifiable moment and at an identifiable location. A release that cannot be traced to a single, identifiable triggering event does not satisfy this requirement. The term \"accidental\" means fortuitous and not the result of deliberate action, inaction, or omission by the Named Insured or any person or entity acting on behalf of, under the direction of, or with the knowledge and consent of the Named Insured.
144	
145	**8. \"Described Premises\"** --- The building and improvements located at 8901 Industrial Parkway, Groveport, OH 43125, as more particularly described on the Declarations Page, together with all land, structures, and fixtures within the property boundaries of the parcel on which the building is situated.
146	
147	**9. \"Business Income\"** --- The sum of:
148	
149	> \(a\) net income (net profit or loss before income taxes) that would have been earned or incurred by the Named Insured; and
150	>
151	> \(b\) continuing normal operating expenses incurred by the Named Insured, including payroll.
152	
153	Business Income does not include any income that would not have been earned had the direct physical loss or damage not occurred, and the Named Insured bears the burden of demonstrating, by reference to historical financial records and other credible evidence, the amount of Business Income that would have been earned during the Period of Restoration.
154	
155	**10. \"Replacement Cost\"** --- The cost to replace Covered Property on the same premises with other property of comparable material and quality, used for the same purpose, without deduction for depreciation. Replacement Cost shall be determined as of the time of repair or replacement, and shall include the cost of labor, materials, and overhead reasonably necessary to complete the repair or replacement. Replacement Cost does not include the cost of any upgrade, improvement, or betterment beyond what is necessary to restore the property to its condition immediately prior to the loss, except as provided under the Ordinance or Law Additional Coverage.
156	
157	**11. \"Actual Cash Value\"** --- The Replacement Cost of Covered Property, less a deduction for depreciation. Depreciation shall be calculated based upon the age, condition, and useful remaining life of the property at the time of loss.
158	
159	**12. \"Deductible\"** --- The amount stated on the Declarations Page (Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$250,000) per occurrence) that the Named Insured must bear before the Insurer\'s obligation to pay under this Policy attaches. The Deductible applies separately to each occurrence and is in addition to any peril-specific deductible stated in this Policy (such as the flood deductible or earthquake deductible). The Insurer\'s payment under this Policy shall be the amount of covered loss in excess of the applicable Deductible, subject to the applicable Limit of Insurance.
160	
161	**[SECTION VII --- CONDITIONS]{.underline}**
162	
163	**[A. Duties in the Event of Loss]{.underline}**
164	
165	In the event of direct physical loss of or damage to Covered Property, or in the event of any occurrence that may give rise to a claim under this Policy, the Named Insured shall comply with the following duties as a condition precedent to the Insurer\'s obligation to pay any claim:
166	
167	**1. Notice.** The Named Insured shall give notice to the Insurer as soon as practicable after a loss, or as soon as practicable after the Named Insured becomes aware of an occurrence that may give rise to a claim under this Policy. Such notice shall include: (a) a description of the Covered Property involved; (b) the time, date, and place of the loss or occurrence; (c) the circumstances giving rise to the loss or occurrence, including the cause of loss to the extent known; and (d) the names and contact information of any witnesses, claimants, or other parties involved. Notice may be given orally and followed by written confirmation, but written notice must be provided to the Insurer within thirty (30) days of the Named Insured\'s initial oral notice.
168	
169	**2. Protection of Property.** The Named Insured shall take all reasonable steps to protect and preserve the Covered Property from further loss or damage, as more fully described in the Sue and Labor provision set forth in Section III of this Policy. The Named Insured\'s duty to protect the Covered Property arises immediately upon the Named Insured\'s awareness of actual or imminent loss, and the Named Insured shall not await instructions from the Insurer before taking protective action. Failure to take reasonable protective measures may reduce or eliminate the Insurer\'s obligation to pay a claim to the extent that such failure results in additional loss or damage that could have been prevented.
170	
171	**3. Cooperation.** The Named Insured shall cooperate fully with the Insurer in the investigation, adjustment, and settlement of any claim arising under this Policy. Cooperation includes, without limitation, providing access to the Described Premises for inspection purposes, providing relevant documents and records, and making the Named Insured\'s officers, managers, employees, and agents available for interviews and examination.
172	
173	**4. Inventory of Damaged Property.** As soon as practicable after a loss, the Named Insured shall prepare and submit to the Insurer a detailed inventory of all damaged, destroyed, or lost Covered Property, showing the quantity, description, original cost, date of acquisition, actual cash value, and replacement cost of each item. The inventory shall be supported by documentation, including purchase records, accounting records, photographs, and other evidence of the property\'s existence and value.
174	
175	**5. Proof of Loss.** Within ninety (90) days after the Insurer\'s written request, the Named Insured shall submit to the Insurer a signed, sworn proof of loss. The proof of loss shall set forth: (a) the time, date, and cause of loss; (b) the interest of the Named Insured and all others in the property involved; (c) the actual cash value and replacement cost of each item of damaged or destroyed property; (d) all other contracts of insurance, whether collectible or not, covering any of the Covered Property; (e) changes in title or occupancy of the Described Premises during the Policy Period; and (f) such other information as the Insurer may reasonably require. The Insurer\'s failure to request a proof of loss shall not waive the Named Insured\'s obligation to provide one if the Insurer subsequently makes such request.
176	
177	**6. Examination Under Oath and Records.** The Named Insured shall, as often as may be reasonably required, submit to examination under oath by any person designated by the Insurer, and shall produce for examination all books of account, business records, bills, invoices, vouchers, and other documents as the Insurer may reasonably request. Such examination may be conducted separately and apart from any examination of other insureds or claimants.
178	
179	**[B. Loss Payment]{.underline}**
180	
181	The Insurer shall pay for covered loss or damage within thirty (30) days after: (a) receiving a satisfactory proof of loss from the Named Insured; and (b) reaching agreement with the Named Insur

If the Insurer and the Named Insured cannot agree on the amount of loss, either party may invoke the Appraisal provision set forth in Section VII.G of this Policy.

Payment shall be made to the Named Insured unless a loss payee, mortgagee, or other payee is designated on the Declarations Page or by endorsement to this Policy. In the event of a loss payable to a mortgagee, the Insurer shall make payment jointly to the Named Insured and the mortgagee, unless otherwise directed by the terms of the applicable mortgage clause.

The Insurer shall have the option, at its sole election, to: (i) pay the value of the lost or damaged Covered Property; (ii) pay the cost of repairing or replacing the lost or damaged Covered Property; (iii) take all or any part of the damaged Covered Property at the agreed or appraised value; or (iv) repair, rebuild, or replace the Covered Property with other property of like kind and quality, with reasonable promptness. The Insurer\'s exercise of any of the foregoing options shall be communicated to the Named Insured in writing within sixty (60) days of the Insurer\'s receipt of a satisfactory proof of loss.

**[C. Valuation]{.underline}**

The value of Covered Property for purposes of loss adjustment shall be determined as follows:

**Building and Business Personal Property.** Building (Coverage A) and business personal property (Coverage B) shall be valued at Replacement Cost, subject to the Coinsurance provision set forth in Section VII.D of this Policy. If the Named Insured elects not to repair or replace the damaged Covered Property, the valuation shall be at Actual Cash Value.

**Stock.** Stock (goods held for storage, distribution, or sale) shall be valued at selling price, less all discounts and charges to which the stock would have been subject had no loss occurred, including shipping costs, sales commissions, and similar expenses not incurred.

**Business Interruption.** Business Income loss under Coverage C shall be valued at the Actual Loss Sustained by the Named Insured during the Period of Restoration, calculated in accordance with the definition of Business Income set forth in Section VI of this Policy, not to exceed the Limit of Insurance stated on the Declarations Page for Coverage C.

**[D. Coinsurance]{.underline}**

This Policy is subject to a coinsurance clause of ninety percent (90%). The Named Insured agrees to maintain insurance under this Policy in an amount equal to at least ninety percent (90%) of the Replacement Cost of Covered Property at the time of loss. If, at the time of loss, the total amount of insurance in effect under this Policy is less than ninety percent (90%) of the Replacement Cost of the Covered Property, the Named Insured shall bear a proportionate share of the loss in accordance with the following formula:

> **Amount of Insurance Carried ÷ (90% × Replacement Cost at Time of Loss) = Percentage of Loss Recoverable**

The Named Insured shall then bear the difference between the full amount of the loss and the amount determined by the foregoing formula. In no event shall the Insurer\'s payment under this coinsurance provision exceed the applicable Limit of Insurance. The coinsurance provision applies separately to each category of Covered Property (building and business personal property) and to each coverage (Coverage A and Coverage B).

**[E. Subrogation]{.underline}**

If the Insurer pays any claim under this Policy, the Insurer shall be subrogated to all of the Named Insured\'s rights of recovery against any party for loss to the extent of the Insurer\'s payment. The Named Insured shall execute and deliver to the Insurer any instruments and papers required and shall cooperate with the Insurer in any action or proceeding necessary to exercise such rights of recovery.

The Named Insured shall not waive, release, or otherwise impair any rights of recovery against any party for loss without the Insurer\'s prior written consent. However, this condition shall not apply to waivers of subrogation that are contained in written contracts or agreements executed by the Named Insured prior to the date of loss, provided that such contracts or agreements were entered into in the ordinary course of the Named Insured\'s business.

**[F. Other Insurance]{.underline}**

If there is other insurance covering the same Covered Property for the same Covered Cause of Loss, this Policy shall pay only its proportionate share of the loss. The Insurer\'s proportionate share shall be the proportion that the applicable Limit of Insurance under this Policy bears to the total amount of all valid and collectible insurance covering the same loss.

If the other insurance is written as primary insurance and this Policy is written as excess insurance (or vice versa), the primary insurance shall pay first, and this Policy shall be excess over the amount of the primary insurance, regardless of any contrary provision in the other policy.

**[G. Appraisal]{.underline}**

If the Named Insured and the Insurer fail to agree on the amount of loss, either party may demand an appraisal of the loss by providing written notice to the other party. Within twenty (20) days after receipt of such notice, each party shall select a competent and disinterested appraiser and notify the other party of the appraiser selected. The two appraisers shall then select a competent and disinterested umpire. If the two appraisers are unable to agree on an umpire within fifteen (15) days, either party may request that a judge of a court of record in the state where the Described Premises is located select an umpire.

The appraisers shall then separately appraise the amount of loss. If the appraisers submit a written report of an agreement, the agreed amount shall be the amount of the loss. If the appraisers fail to agree, they shall submit their differences to the umpire. A decision agreed to by any two of the three (the two appraisers and the umpire) shall be binding on both parties. Each party shall bear the expense of its own appraiser, and the parties shall share equally the expense of the umpire. The appraisal process shall determine only the amount of the loss and shall not determine any question of coverage or liability under this Policy.

**[H. Liberalization]{.underline}**

If, during the Policy Period or within sixty (60) days prior to the inception of the Policy Period, the Insurer adopts any revision to the policy forms used in connection with this type of insurance that would broaden the coverage afforded under this Policy without additional premium, such broadened coverage shall immediately and automatically apply to this Policy as of the date of adoption by the Insurer.

**[I. Concealment, Misrepresentation, or Fraud]{.underline}**

This entire Policy shall be void if, whether before or after a loss, the Named Insured has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance relating to this insurance, the Covered Property, or any claim submitted under this Policy. A misrepresentation is material if the Insurer would not have issued this Policy, or would have issued it on different terms, had it known the true facts.

**[J. Cancellation and Nonrenewal]{.underline}**

**Cancellation by Named Insured.** The Named Insured may cancel this Policy at any time by providing written notice of cancellation to the Insurer. Cancellation shall be effective on the date specified in the notice, or if no date is specified, on the date the notice is received by the Insurer.

**Cancellation by Insurer.** The Insurer may cancel this Policy by providing the Named Insured with written notice of cancellation, mailed or delivered to the Named Insured\'s mailing address shown on the Declarations Page. If cancellation is for nonpayment of premium, the Insurer shall provide at least ten (10) days\' advance written notice. For all other reasons, the Insurer shall provide at least thirty (30) days\' advance written notice. Cancellation shall be effective at 12:01 A.M. standard time at the Named Insured\'s mailing address on the date specified in the notice.

**Nonrenewal.** If the Insurer elects not to renew this Policy, the Insurer shall provide the Named Insured with written notice of nonrenewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the Policy Period. Failure to provide timely notice of nonrenewal shall result in the automatic renewal of this Policy for an additional one-year period on the same terms and conditions, subject to the Insurer\'s right to adjust the premium in accordance with applicable rating schedules.

**Return Premium.** If this Policy is cancelled, the earned premium shall be computed on a pro rata basis for the period during which the Policy was in force. Any unearned premium shall be returned to the Named Insured within thirty (30) days of the effective date of cancellation.

**[K. Transfer of Rights and Duties]{.underline}**

The rights and duties under this Policy may not be transferred, assigned, or conveyed to any other person or organization without the prior written consent of the Insurer, which consent may be withheld in the Insurer\'s sole discretion. Any purported transfer, assignment, or conveyance without such consent shall be void and of no effect.

In the event of the death of an individual Named Insured, the Named Insured\'s rights and duties under this Policy shall automatically vest in the Named Insured\'s legal representative, but only while acting within the scope of duties as legal representative. Coverage shall continue until the expiration of the Policy Period.

**[L. Legal Action Against the Insurer]{.underline}**

No person or organization shall have the right to bring any legal action, suit, or proceeding against the Insurer under this Policy unless: (i) there has been full compliance with all of the terms, conditions, and duties set forth in this Policy; and (ii) the action is brought within two (2) years after the date on which the direct physical loss or damage occurred. Any action brought after the expiration of this two-year period shall be barred, regardless of the date on which the Named Insured first became aware of the loss or damage.

**Venue.** Any suit, action, or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Policy shall be brought exclusively in a court of competent jurisdiction located in Franklin County, Ohio. The Named Insured and the Insurer each consent to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the courts of Franklin County, Ohio for any such suit, action, or proceeding.

**Governing Law.** This Policy shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Ohio, without giving effect to any choice-of-law or conflict-of-laws rules that would require the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

**[M. Mortgage Holders / Loss Payable]{.underline}**

**Standard Mortgagee Clause.** If a mortgagee is named on the Declarations Page or by endorsement to this Policy, any loss payable under Coverage A --- Building shall be paid to the mortgagee (subject to the terms of this clause), as the mortgagee\'s interest may appear, and the mortgagee\'s interest in this Policy shall not be invalidated by any act or neglect of the Named Insured. However, if the Named Insured fails to submit a proof of loss within the time required, the mortgagee must do so within sixty (60) days after receiving notice from the Insurer of the Named Insured\'s failure. The mortgagee shall notify the Insurer of any change in ownership, occupancy, or substantial increase in hazard of which the mortgagee is aware. If the Insurer cancels this Policy, the Insurer shall give the mortgagee at least ten (10) days\' written notice of cancellation.

**Loss Payable Clause.** If a loss payee is named on the Declarations Page or by endorsement to this Policy, any loss payable under Coverage B --- Business Personal Property shall be adjusted with the Named Insured and payable jointly to the Named Insured and the designated loss payee, as their interests may appear. The loss payee\'s interest in this Policy is subject to all of the terms, conditions, and exclusions of this Policy.

**[SECTION VIII --- TERRITORIAL SCOPE]{.underline}**

**Primary Territory.** This Policy applies to Covered Property at the Described Premises located at 8901 Industrial Parkway, Groveport, OH 43125. All coverages provided under this Policy, including Coverage A --- Building, Coverage B --- Business Personal Property, Coverage C --- Business Interruption / Loss of Income, and all Additional Coverages, apply to Covered Property at the Described Premises.

**Extended Territory.** In addition to coverage at the Described Premises, this Policy also applies to business personal property of the Named Insured while temporarily located at any location within the continental United States, provided that such property is:

> \(a\) in transit to or from the Described Premises in the ordinary course of the Named Insured\'s warehousing and distribution business; or
>
> \(b\) temporarily stored at such other location in the ordinary course of the Named Insured\'s business, including at customer facilities, third-party warehouses, cross-dock facilities, or similar locations where property is held pending further distribution or return to the Described Premises.

The extended territory coverage for off-premises business personal property is subject to a sublimit of Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) at any single off-premises location within the extended territory. The Named Insured shall maintain records of all business personal property at off-premises locations and shall make such records available to the Insurer upon request.

**Limitations on Extended Territory.** The extended territory provision set forth above does not apply to the following coverages, which apply only at the Described Premises:

> \(a\) Flood coverage (Section IV.B and Section IX);
>
> \(b\) Earthquake coverage (Section IV.C and Section IX); and
>
> \(c\) Equipment Breakdown Additional Coverage (Section II.D).

**Property in Transit.** Business personal property is covered while in transit within the continental United States from the time it leaves the Described Premises until it is delivered to the Named Insured\'s customer or returned to the Described Premises. Property in transit is covered against all Covered Causes of Loss, subject to the standard per-occurrence Deductible and the off-premises sublimit stated above.

The continental United States, for purposes of this Section VIII, means the forty-eight contiguous states of the United States and the District of Columbia, but does not include Alaska, Hawaii, or any territory or possession of the United States.

**[SECTION IX --- LOSS CONDITIONS SPECIFIC TO FLOOD AND EARTHQUAKE]{.underline}**

**[Flood Loss Conditions]{.underline}**

The following conditions apply exclusively to losses caused by or resulting from the peril of Flood, as defined in Section IV.B of this Policy:

1\. **Single Flood Occurrence.** All flood losses occurring within any continuous period of one hundred sixty-eight hours (168 hours or seven days) shall constitute a single flood occurrence for purposes of applying the flood deductible and the annual aggregate sublimit. The Named Insured shall select the starting date and time of the 168-hour period, subject to the requirement that the period must commence no earlier than the time at which flood waters first contact the Described Premises or Covered Property.

2\. **Annual Aggregate Sublimit.** The maximum amount payable for all flood losses occurring during the Policy Period shall not exceed Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) in the annual aggregate. Payments for flood losses shall be applied against this annual aggregate sublimit as they are made, and the remaining available sublimit shall be reduced accordingly. Once the aggregate sublimit is exhausted, no further flood losses shall be covered under this Policy for the remainder of the Policy Period.

3\. **Flood Deductible.** In addition to the standard per-occurrence Deductible of \$250,000 stated on the Declarations Page, a separate flood deductible of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per flood occurrence shall apply. The flood deductible is applied after the standard per-occurrence Deductible. Accordingly, the total amount the Named Insured must bear before the Insurer\'s obligation to pay for a flood loss attaches is Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$750,000) per flood occurrence.

4\. **NFIP Compliance.** The Named Insured shall comply with all applicable requirements of the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), including maintaining any NFIP policy required by law, regulation, or the terms of any mortgage or loan agreement applicable to the Described Premises.

**[Earthquake Loss Conditions]{.underline}**

The following conditions apply exclusively to losses caused by or resulting from the peril of Earthquake, as defined in Section IV.C of this Policy:

1\. **Single Earthquake Occurrence.** All earthquake shocks occurring within any continuous period of one hundred sixty-eight hours (168 hours or seven days) shall constitute a single earthquake occurrence for purposes of applying the earthquake deductible and the annual aggregate sublimit. The 168-hour period shall commence at the time of the first earthquake shock.

2\. **Annual Aggregate Sublimit.** The maximum amount payable for all earthquake losses occurring during the Policy Period shall not exceed Three Million Dollars (\$3,000,000) in the annual aggregate. Payments for earthquake losses shall be applied against this annual aggregate sublimit as they are made, and the remaining available sublimit shall be reduced accordingly. Once the aggregate sublimit is exhausted, no further earthquake losses shall be covered under this Policy for the remainder of the Policy Period.

3\. **Earthquake Deductible.** In addition to the standard per-occurrence Deductible of \$250,000 stated on the Declarations Page, a separate earthquake deductible shall apply to each earthquake occurrence. The earthquake deductible shall be equal to two percent (2%) of the applicable Coverage A or Coverage B Limit of Insurance, subject to a minimum earthquake deductible of Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$250,000) per earthquake occurrence. For the avoidance of doubt, the earthquake deductible is calculated on the full Coverage A or Coverage B Limit, not on the earthquake sublimit.

4\. **Application to Described Premises Only.** Earthquake coverage under this Policy applies only to Covered Property located at the Described Premises and does not extend to business personal property at off-premises locations covered under the extended territory provisions of Coverage B or Section VIII.

**[SECTION X --- ENDORSEMENTS]{.underline}**

**[Endorsement No. 1 --- Equipment Breakdown Coverage]{.underline}**

**Endorsement No. 1** **Policy No. BM-CP-2024-07821** **Effective Date: March 1, 2024**

This Endorsement modifies the coverage provided under Policy No. BM-CP-2024-07821 issued by Blackwater Mutual Insurance Company. All other terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations of the Policy remain unchanged except as specifically modified herein.

**Equipment Breakdown as a Covered Cause of Loss.** Equipment breakdown is added as a Covered Cause of Loss under this Policy. For purposes of this Endorsement, \"equipment breakdown\" means the sudden and accidental failure or breakdown of electrical, mechanical, or pressure equipment that is owned by the Named Insured or in the Named Insured\'s care, custody, or control, and that is located at the Described Premises.

**Sublimit.** The maximum amount payable for any single equipment breakdown occurrence under this Endorsement shall not exceed Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000).

**Spoilage of Perishable Goods.** This Endorsement includes coverage for the spoilage of perishable goods stored in the cold-storage facility at the Described Premises resulting directly from an equipment breakdown, including loss of perishable goods due to temperature change caused by failure of refrigeration compressors, condensers, evaporators, or related equipment. This coverage also extends to contamination of perishable goods resulting from ammonia leakage caused by the breakdown of ammonia-based refrigeration equipment.

**Deductible.** A separate deductible of Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$50,000) per equipment breakdown occurrence applies to claims under this Endorsement. This deductible is in lieu of (and not in addition to) the standard per-occurrence Deductible stated on the Declarations Page.

**Exclusions.** This Equipment Breakdown coverage does not apply to loss or damage caused by or resulting from: (a) gradual deterioration, corrosion, wear and tear, or depletion; (b) scheduled or routine maintenance or testing; (c) breakdown of equipment that has been removed from service and is not being maintained in operable condition; or (d) any cause of loss that would be covered under Coverage A or Coverage B independent of this Endorsement (in which case, the standard Policy provisions apply).

**[Endorsement No. 2 --- Ordinance or Law Coverage Enhancement]{.underline}**

**Endorsement No. 2** **Policy No. BM-CP-2024-07821** **Effective Date: March 1, 2024**

This Endorsement modifies the coverage provided under Policy No. BM-CP-2024-07821 issued by Blackwater Mutual Insurance Company. All other terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations of the Policy remain unchanged except as specifically modified herein.

**Enhanced Ordinance or Law Coverage.** The Ordinance or Law Additional Coverage set forth in Section II.B of the Policy is hereby enhanced to provide a sublimit of Four Million Dollars (\$4,000,000) per occurrence for the combined total of all three subcoverages (loss in value of undamaged portion, demolition cost, and increased cost of construction).

**Scope of Coverage.** This Endorsement applies to loss resulting from the enforcement of building codes, zoning laws, fire codes, safety regulations, or other ordinances or regulations enacted by governmental bodies having jurisdiction over the Described Premises. Coverage under this Endorsement includes the increased cost of construction necessary to comply with current building codes and standards in effect at the time of repair, rebuilding, or replacement of the building at the Described Premises.

**Conditions.** The Named Insured must commence repair, rebuilding, or replacement of the damaged building within two (2) years of the date of loss to be eligible for reimbursement of increased construction costs under this Endorsement. If the Named Insured fails to commence repair, rebuilding, or replacement within this two-year period, coverage under this Endorsement shall be limited to the loss in value of the undamaged portion of the building.

**[Endorsement No. 3 --- Terrorism Risk Insurance Act (TRIA) Disclosure]{.underline}**

**Endorsement No. 3** **Policy No. BM-CP-2024-07821** **Effective Date: March 1, 2024**

This Endorsement is issued in compliance with the Terrorism Risk Insurance Act of 2002 (TRIA), as amended by the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Reauthorization Act of 2019 (Public Law 116-94).

**Disclosure of Terrorism Coverage.** In accordance with TRIA, the Insurer hereby discloses that this Policy includes coverage for insured losses resulting from \"certified acts of terrorism\" as defined in Section 102(1) of TRIA, as amended. A \"certified act of terrorism\" means an act that is certified by the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Attorney General of the United States, to be an act of terrorism.

**Federal Participation.** Under TRIA, the United States Government will pay a share of terrorism losses insured under federal terrorism insurance programs. The federal share of compensation equals a percentage of insured losses that exceeds the applicable insurer deductible, as determined under TRIA. The specific percentage of the federal share and the insurer\'s deductible are established annually by the Secretary of the Treasury.

**Insurer Deductible.** The Insurer is responsible for a deductible under TRIA before federal assistance becomes available. The deductible is calculated as a percentage of the Insurer\'s direct earned premiums for the preceding calendar year.

**Policyholder Premium.** The portion of the premium attributable to terrorism coverage under this Endorsement is identified separately in the premium schedule attached to this Policy.

**Named Insured\'s Election.** The Named Insured acknowledges receipt of this TRIA disclosure and has elected to maintain terrorism coverage under this Policy. The Named Insured\'s signature on the Declarations Page constitutes acknowledgment and acceptance of this disclosure.

**[Endorsement No. 4 --- Waiver of Subrogation]{.underline}**

**Endorsement No. 4** **Policy No. BM-CP-2024-07821** **Effective Date: March 1, 2024**

This Endorsement modifies the Subrogation provision set forth in Section VII.E of the Policy. All other terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations of the Policy remain unchanged except as specifically modified herein.

**Waiver of Subrogation.** The Insurer waives any right of subrogation it may have against any person or organization with whom the Named Insured has entered into a written contract or agreement requiring such waiver, provided that the written contract or agreement was executed by the Named Insured prior to the date of the direct physical loss or damage giving rise to the claim under this Policy. This waiver of subrogation does not apply to any loss or damage caused by the intentional acts of the person or organization in whose favor the waiver is granted.

**[SECTION XI --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**[A. Entire Agreement]{.underline}**

This Policy, including the Declarations Page and all endorsements and forms listed thereon, constitutes the entire agreement between the Named Insured and the Insurer with respect to the insurance provided herein. No change, amendment, or modification of this Policy shall be valid or effective unless made by written endorsement issued by the Insurer and attached to this Policy. No oral statement or representation made by or to any agent, broker, or representative of the Insurer shall be deemed to modify, waive, or extend any provision of this Policy.

**[B. Conformity to Statute]{.underline}**

If any provision of this Policy is in conflict with the applicable statutes of the State of Ohio, this Policy is hereby amended to conform to such statutes. Any provision required by Ohio law to be included in this Policy shall be deemed to be incorporated herein, whether or not expressly set forth.

**[C. Inspections]{.underline}**

The Insurer shall have the right, but not the obligation, to inspect the Named Insured\'s premises, operations, equipment, and records at any reasonable time during the Policy Period. Neither the Insurer\'s right to inspect nor the actual performance of any inspection constitutes an undertaking, on behalf of or for the benefit of the Named Insured or any other party, to determine or warrant that the Described Premises or the Named Insured\'s operations are safe, healthful, or in compliance with any law, regulation, code, or standard.

**[D. Recoveries]{.underline}**

Any recoveries obtained from third parties after payment of a loss under this Policy, whether by subrogation, salvage, or otherwise, shall be applied in the following order: (a) first, to reimburse the Insurer for its payment under this Policy; (b) second, to reimburse the Named Insured for the Deductible or any other amount borne by the Named Insured; and (c) third, to reimburse the Named Insured for any excess loss not covered under this Policy. The costs and expenses of obtaining any such recovery shall be borne proportionately by the Insurer and the Named Insured in the ratio of their respective interests in the recovery.

**[E. Policy Modification]{.underline}**

Only duly authorized officers and representatives of the Insurer have authority to modify, amend, extend, or waive any term, condition, or provision of this Policy. No agent, broker, or other intermediary has the authority to alter, modify, or waive any condition or provision of this Policy, or to extend the time for payment of premium, or to bind the Insurer by any promise or representation not contained in this Policy.

**[SIGNATURE PAGE]{.underline}**

**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, Blackwater Mutual Insurance Company has caused this Policy to be executed and attested by its duly authorized officers as of the effective date shown on the Declarations Page.

This Policy, including the Declarations Page, Sections I through XI, and all Endorsements attached hereto, takes effect on March 1, 2024, at 12:01 A.M. standard time at the Named Insured\'s mailing address, and remains in force until February 28, 2025, at 12:01 A.M. standard time at the Named Insured\'s mailing address, unless sooner cancelled or terminated in accordance with the provisions of this Policy.

  **Estimated Ceding Commission**                  \$27,520,000

  **Estimated Net Premium Payable to Reinsurer**   \$58,480,000

  **Payment Terms**                                Quarterly installments, due within 45 days of the close of each calendar quarter
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Subject premium excludes supplementary or additional coverage amounts. Adjustments to ceded premium shall be calculated at the close of each calendar quarter based on actual gross written premium for Treaty-eligible lines, with a final adjustment within 90 days of the expiration of each annual period. Minimum and deposit premium provisions apply as set forth in the Treaty wording.

**[9. EXCLUSIONS]{.underline}**

The following perils, risks, and classes of business are excluded from the scope of this Treaty:

> \(a\) Terrorism as defined under the Terrorism Risk Insurance Act (TRIA), as amended, and any successor legislation thereto;
>
> \(b\) Cyber and electronic risks, including but not limited to losses arising from unauthorized access to, or the failure of, computer systems, networks, or data;
>
> \(c\) War, invasion, acts of foreign enemies, hostilities (whether war be declared or not), civil war, rebellion, revolution, insurrection, military or usurped power, and nuclear risks including nuclear reaction, radiation, or radioactive contamination;
>
> \(d\) Asbestos and environmental pollution, except sudden and accidental pollution;
>
> \(e\) Flood and earthquake perils;
>
> \(f\) Governmental action or order, including but not limited to confiscation, nationalization, seizure, or destruction by any government or public authority.

**[10. OCCURRENCE DEFINITION]{.underline}**

Each individual loss event, as determined by the 72-hour clause. All individual losses arising from a continuous or related cause within any consecutive 72-hour period shall be deemed a single occurrence. The selection of the 72-hour period shall be made by the Reassured so as to maximize recovery hereunder.

**[11. CLAIMS]{.underline}**

**Notice Requirement:** The Reassured shall provide written notice to the Reinsurer, through the Intermediary, of any claim or occurrence likely to give rise to a recovery hereunder in excess of \$500,000 (Reinsurer\'s share) within 15 business days of the Reassured\'s receipt of notice from the insured or its knowledge of such claim or occurrence, whichever is earlier.

**Claims Cooperation:** The Reinsurer shall have the right to associate in the defense, investigation, and adjustment of any claim where the Reinsurer\'s potential exposure exceeds \$2,000,000 (equivalent to \$5,000,000 on a gross basis). Such association shall be at the Reinsurer\'s own expense and shall not prejudice the Reassured\'s control of the claim.

**Follow the Fortunes:** The Reinsurer shall follow the fortunes of the Reassured in all matters relating to the adjustment, settlement, and payment of claims arising under policies reinsured hereunder, provided that such claims fall within the terms and conditions of this Treaty and that the Reassured has acted in good faith and in a businesslike manner.

**ECO/XPL:** Extra-contractual obligations (ECO) and excess of policy limits (XPL) losses are covered hereunder, subject to a maximum of \$10,000,000 per occurrence, provided the underlying loss (exclusive of ECO/XPL) falls within the terms of this Treaty.

**[12. BUSINESS INTERRUPTION]{.underline}**

Business interruption losses are covered hereunder, subject to an indemnity period not exceeding 6 months from the date of loss.

**[13. OFFSET]{.underline}**

The Reassured shall have the right to offset any amounts owed by the Reassured to the Reinsurer against any amounts owed by the Reinsurer to the Reassured under this Treaty. Such offset may be applied to balances arising under any provision of this Treaty, including but not limited to premiums, claims, commissions, and return premiums.

**[14. INSOLVENCY]{.underline}**

In the event of the Reassured\'s insolvency, the Reinsurer\'s obligations hereunder shall be payable directly to the liquidator, rehabilitator, receiver, or statutory successor of the Reassured, without diminution because of the insolvency. All claims under this Treaty must be filed with the Reinsurer within 24 months of the entry of the insolvency order. The insolvency provisions of this Treaty shall be interpreted in accordance with Ohio Revised Code § 3903.01 et seq. and applicable Bermuda law.

**[15. DISPUTE RESOLUTION]{.underline}**

Any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Treaty, including any question regarding its existence, validity, or termination, shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration seated in Bermuda. The arbitration panel shall consist of three arbitrators, each of whom shall be a current or former officer of an insurance or reinsurance company. The arbitration shall be conducted under the rules of the Bermuda International Conciliation and Arbitration Act 1993. The panel shall make its decision having regard to the custom and practice of the insurance and reinsurance industry (honorable engagement clause) and shall not be obliged to follow the strict rules of law.

**[16. GOVERNING LAW]{.underline}**

This Treaty shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of Bermuda.

**[17. INTERMEDIARY CLAUSE]{.underline}**

Ridgeline Broking Ltd. acts as intermediary in respect of this Treaty. All communications between the Reassured and the Reinsurer, including but not limited to premium remittances, claims advices, claims payments, and all notices required hereunder, shall flow through and be transmitted by Ridgeline Broking Ltd. Ridgeline Broking Ltd. shall hold all funds received in connection with this Treaty in a fiduciary capacity in accordance with applicable law and regulation.
